title: Phase 4 Atrioventricular Block Following Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: Unmasking Latent Conduction Disease.
authors: Shivani Reddy; Ariane T Lemieux; Alan Donsky; Manish Assar; Robert C Stoler
abstract: Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) carries up to a 15% risk of complete heart block (CHB) within 30 days, but the mechanisms driving recurrent heart block after the apparent initial conduction system recovery post-TAVR remain incompletely understood. Phase 4 atrioventricular block, a pause-dependent phenomenon occurring when supraventricular or ventricular impulses encounter diseased His-Purkinje fibers during diastolic depolarization, may contribute to post-TAVR conduction disturbances. We present an instructive case of a 71-year-old woman with severe aortic valve stenosis who developed CHB in the setting of phase 4 atrioventricular block following TAVR. Despite recovering sinus rhythm with 1:1 atrioventricular conduction within 12 hours post-procedure, she experienced recurrent ventricular standstill upon temporary pacemaker removal, ultimately requiring permanent pacemaker implantation. This case illustrates the multiple mechanisms and temporal patterns of post-TAVR conduction system disorders, the potential unreliability of early apparent conduction recovery as a predictor of durable atrioventricular conduction, and the necessity for careful and more prolonged patient monitoring before and after temporary pacemaker removal.

title: Surgical outcomes of infective endocarditis in children and adults with congenital heart disease.
authors: Thibault Schaeffer; Kenan Alaham; Doris Kienmoser; Andrea Amici; Jonas Palm; Teresa Lemmen; Christina Ruda; Nicole Piber; Muneaki Matsubara; Paul Philipp Heinisch; Alfred Hager; Peter Ewert; Jürgen Hörer; Masamichi Ono
journal: The Journal of thoracic and cardiovascular surgery
abstract:
Reports describing surgery for infective endocarditis (IE) in children and adults with congenital heart disease (CHD) are limited. This study aimed to determine the patient characteristics, preoperative conditions, surgical outcomes, and risk factors in this cohort.
All children and adults with CHD who underwent surgical treatment for IE between 2001 and 2024 were reviewed. Patient characteristics and surgical procedures were evaluated; survival, recurrent IE, and risk factors were analyzed.
A total of 96 patients underwent surgical treatment for IE, including 52 children and 44 adults with CHD. Underlying CHD included ventricular septal defect in 31 patients, aortic stenosis/insufficiency in 26, and tetralogy of Fallot in 14. The most frequently infected lesion was the aortic valve in 40 patients, and the most frequently detected organism was Staphylococcus species in 34 patients. Vegetation was observed in 65 patients. Median age at surgery was 17.2 (IQR: 11.7-29.4) years. In-hospital mortality was 6.3%, and survival at 5, 10, and 20 years was 90.6, 88.1, and 80.5%, respectively. Freedom from recurrent IE was 96.4% at 20 years. Number of previous operations (hazard ratio (HR): 1.585, p=0.005), gram-negative bacteria (HR: 11.475, p<0.001), emergency operations (HR: 17.988, p=0.001), and longer aortic cross-clamp time (HR: 1.011, p=0.043) were risk factors for mortality.
In children and adults with CHD, mortality following surgery for IE was low, and recurrent IE was rare. Individualized management based on the patient's preoperative condition and the causative organism appears to be important for improving survival.

title: Multilayer regulation of osteogenic reprogramming in human aortic valve interstitial cells in calcific aortic valve disease.
authors: Chunyang Liang; Linwen Zhu; Min Zhou; Huoshun Shi; Guofeng Shao
abstract: Calcific aortic valve disease (CAVD) is an active fibrocalcific disorder in which human aortic valve interstitial cells (hVICs) undergo heterogeneous osteogenic reprogramming. This narrative review provides an hVIC-centered synthesis of four interacting regulatory layers: pathological microenvironmental cues, intracellular signaling, non-coding RNA regulation, and cellular heterogeneity. Lipid dysregulation, inflammation, hypoxia, oxidative and metabolic stress, cellular senescence, and abnormal mechanical loading alter hVIC behavior through interconnected developmental, inflammatory, metabolic, and mechanosensitive pathways. Non-coding RNAs add post-transcriptional and epigenetic regulation, although many proposed axes remain incompletely validated. Single-cell transcriptomic studies further identify distinct disease-associated hVIC states and challenge a universal linear transition from quiescent to myofibroblast-like and osteogenic cells. We compare conventional and advanced experimental models and evaluate emerging therapeutic strategies according to the strength of human, functional, and translational evidence. Current data support a context- and stage-dependent network rather than a single dominant pathway. Integrating human valve tissue, cell-state-resolved analyses, complementary disease models, clinically meaningful endpoints, and targeted delivery may improve biomarker development and support disease-modifying strategies for CAVD.

title: Machine Learning-Based Clustering of Clinical Phenotypes in Adults With Bicuspid Aortic Valve: A Large Single-Center Study.
authors: Xinyue Zhang; Zhuo Chen; Zhaokai Xu; Tingting Liu; Lixin Zhang; Yihua He; Xiaoyan Gu
abstract:
Bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) is clinically heterogeneous, and the relationships among valve morphology, valvular dysfunction, and aortic involvement remain incompletely understood. We aimed to identify clinical phenotypes of adults with BAV by clustering multidimensional clinical data, primarily echocardiographic parameters.
We retrospectively included adults with echocardiographically confirmed BAV at Beijing Anzhen Hospital between January 2016 and December 2024. Data from the first echocardiographic examination and contemporaneous clinical records were extracted, and nine continuous and three categorical variables were entered into a two-step clustering model. Continuous and categorical variables were compared across clusters using the Kruskal-Wallis H test and chi-square test, respectively, followed by pairwise comparisons. The stability of the four-cluster solution was assessed using 100 bootstrap resamples; agreement was quantified with the adjusted Rand index (ARI) and Jaccard coefficients. Clustering was also repeated after separately excluding sex and valve dysfunction to assess the influence of these key variables on cluster structure.
A total of 6977 patients with echocardiographically diagnosed BAV were included. The median age was 53.0 years (interquartile range, 40.0-61.0), and 70.0% were men. Two-step clustering identified four clinical phenotypes that differed significantly in valve morphology, valvular dysfunction, aortic dimensions, left-heart remodeling, cardiac function, and surgical interventions (all p < 0.001): Cluster 1, a predominantly male, regurgitation-predominant phenotype with left ventricular dilatation; Cluster 2, a predominantly male, stenosis-predominant phenotype with concentric hypertrophy; Cluster 3, a male phenotype with no or mild valve dysfunction; and Cluster 4, a female phenotype characterized mainly by no or mild valve dysfunction with a tendency toward stenosis. The proportion undergoing subsequent surgery after the baseline echocardiographic assessment was highest in Cluster 2 (40%) and lowest in Cluster 3 (14%). Left ventricular end-systolic diameter, left ventricular end-diastolic diameter, aortic root diameter, valve dysfunction, and sex were the principal drivers of clustering. Across bootstrap resamples, the mean ARI for the four-cluster solution was 0.696. In sensitivity analyses, exclusion of either sex or valve dysfunction reduced the optimal solution from four clusters to two.
Machine learning-based two-step clustering identified four baseline clinical phenotypes among adults with BAV, revealing multidimensional combinations of valve morphology, valvular function, aortic dimensions, and left-heart remodeling. This classification is intended primarily to characterize the clinical heterogeneity of adult BAV; its longitudinal clinical value requires confirmation in independent prospective cohorts.

title: Dynamic Transmitral Gradient From Eccentric Aortic Regurgitation Resolved by Valve-in-Valve TAVR.
authors: Ishita Ray; Sami Shoura; Ragavendar Saravanabavanandan; Kyle Coombes; Rajvardhan Sisodia; Michael Z Grzeskowiak; Sudhir Mungee; Marco A Barzallo
abstract:
Bioprosthetic aortic valve degeneration can present as isolated regurgitant failure, and an eccentric jet may raise the transmitral gradient, mimicking mitral stenosis.
An 84-year-old man presented with acute heart failure 12 years after surgical aortic valve replacement. Echocardiography showed a degenerated Trifecta bioprosthesis with an immobile leaflet causing severe eccentric aortic regurgitation, whose jet impinged on the anterior mitral leaflet and produced severe functional mitral stenosis. Given high surgical risk, the heart team performed transfemoral valve-in-valve transcatheter aortic valve replacement.
Trifecta leaflet tear causes regurgitant rather than stenotic failure; an eccentric jet can raise the transmitral gradient independent of the Austin Flint murmur. Valve-in-valve transcatheter aortic valve replacement eliminated the regurgitation, improved leaflet mobility, and reduced the mean mitral gradient from 17 to 6 mm Hg, with complete symptom resolution.
Eccentric aortic regurgitation can cause a reversible rise in transmitral gradient; treating it can resolve apparent mitral stenosis without mitral intervention.

title: CT-Based Deep Learning Assessment of Aortic Valve Fibrosis and Calcification: Development and Multicenter External Validation Against Experts, Histology, and Outcomes.
authors: Kajetan Grodecki; Nipun Manral; Jacek Kwiecinski; Joel Lenell; Sebastien Cadet; Tara Zuhair Kassem; Jolien Geers; Caroline Park; Emily Xing; Guadalupe Flores Tomasino; Anna Olasinska-Wisniewska; Rafal Wolny; Maciej Dabrowski; Marcin Protasiewicz; Zbigniew Chmielak; Wojciech Wojakowski; Julia Niemierko; Jadwiga Fijalkowska; Bartosz Rymuza; Radoslaw Parma; Piotr Scislo; Marcin Grabowski; Dariusz Jagielak; Andrzej Walczak; Adrianna Hajder; Matylda Grodecka; Radoslaw Gocol; Tomasz Urbanowicz; Bartłomiej Perek; Marek Jemielity; Krzysztof Reczuch; Marek Grygier; Philipp Ruile; Simon Schoechlin; Hesham Elzomor; Michelle C Williams; Marc R Dweck; Daniel S Berman; David E Newby; Janusz Kochman; Hasan Jilaihawi; Raj Makkar; Piotr J Slomka; Adam Witkowski; Zenon Huczek; Damini Dey
abstract:
Computed tomography angiography (CTA) enables assessment of aortic valve tissue composition, providing insights into disease progression and helping predict outcomes in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement for severe aortic stenosis (AS). The authors aimed to develop a deep learning system for CTA-based quantification of aortic fibrotic and calcific tissue, validate its agreement with expert manual analysis and histopathology, and evaluate its value for outcome prediction.
This international, multicenter study included 1,674 patients who underwent CTA at 9 sites. A deep learning model based on the nnU-Net architecture was trained in 468 patients and applied to an external test set of 1,206 patients, including 29 with valve histology and 12 with serial CTA. In 1,165 patients with clinical outcomes, prognostic value was assessed adjusting for clinical, echocardiographic, and procedural covariates.
Deep learning-enabled tissue composition analysis was rapid (1.35 ± 0.4 min vs 7.2 ± 1.2 min for experts) with excellent agreement vs expert assessment (r = 0.915; intraclass correlation coefficient [ICC] = 0.913), histology (r = 0.909; ICC = 0.905), and scan-rescan reproducibility (r = 0.999; ICC = 0.999). In the external cohort, 469 patients (40%) died over 4.1 ± 1.1 years of follow-up. Fibrotic tissue volume (adjusted HR [aHR] 1.42 per IQR increase; P < 0.001), calcific tissue attenuation (aHR 1.02 per 25 HU increase; P = 0.005), left ventricular ejection fraction (aHR 1.10 per 5% decrease; P < 0.001), life-threatening bleeding (aHR: 1.96; P = 0.003), major vascular complication (aHR: 1.51; P = 0.042) and postprocedural peak pressure gradient (aHR 1.03 per 1 mm Hg increase; P < 0.001) independently predicted mortality. Patients in the highest tertile of fibrotic tissue volume (>0.940 cm3) had a 2-fold higher risk of death (aHR: 2.0; P < 0.001), whereas patients with dense calcific tissue attenuation (>885 HU) had a 1.5-fold higher risk of death.
Deep learning enables rapid quantification of aortic valve fibrotic and calcific tissue from CTA, demonstrating excellent agreement with both expert CTA and histological assessments. Quantitative analysis of aortic tissue composition provides additional prognostic value for all-cause mortality after transcatheter aortic valve replacement in multicenter external evaluation.

title: From Anatomy to Tissue: Cardiac CT Finally Turns Its Attention to the Aortic Valve.
authors: Saima Mushtaq; Gianluca Pontone

title: Percutaneous Rescue of Acute Left Ventricular Outflow Tract Obstruction After Mitral Valve-In-Valve Replacement.
authors: Andrea Mangiameli; Valentina Bernardini; Alessia Azzano; Eligio Miccichè; Elvis Brscic; Andrea Cascella; Rocco Mollace; Davide Cao
journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
abstract:
Left ventricular outflow tract obstruction (LVOTO) is a rare but potentially life-threatening complication of transcatheter mitral valve replacement (TMVR). Mitral valve-in-valve procedures are generally associated with a lower risk of LVOTO because of the predictable geometry provided by the surgical bioprosthesis, yet severe obstruction may still occur and precipitate abrupt hemodynamic collapse.
A 79-year-old woman with a degenerated 27-mm Carpentier-Edwards Perimount mitral bioprosthesis presented with acute decompensated heart failure due to severe bioprosthetic mitral stenosis. Following multidisciplinary Heart Team evaluation, she was considered not a candidate for redo mitral valve surgery and underwent urgent transseptal valve-in-valve TMVR with a 26-mm balloon-expandable SAPIEN valve.
Immediately after valve deployment, severe LVOTO developed, with an invasive peak-to-peak LV-aortic gradient of 120 mmHg. A mechanism-guided percutaneous rescue strategy was undertaken. Correction of the structural component of obstruction reduced the gradient to 60 mmHg. Persistent obstruction suggested a significant dynamic contribution, prompting selective septal branch coil embolization, which further reduced the gradient to 20 mmHg and resulted in immediate hemodynamic stabilization.
Severe LVOTO after valve-in-valve TMVR may reflect both structural and dynamic mechanisms. Persistence of significant obstruction after structural correction should prompt consideration of a dynamic component and may guide effective rescue therapy.

title: Aortic annular enlargement using the Yang technique: the first reported case in the Peruvian Ministry of Health.
authors: Marycielo A Valdez; Edmy Callalli Matos; Silvana Gonzales
journal: Archivos peruanos de cardiologia y cirugia cardiovascular
abstract: Prosthesis-patient mismatch (PPM) remains an important limitation in patients with a small aortic annulus undergoing surgical aortic valve replacement. The Yang technique (Y-incision) has recently emerged as an effective alternative for achieving greater aortic annular enlargement while maintaining favorable perioperative outcomes. We report the first case of aortic annular enlargement using the Yang technique performed at our institution in a 56-year-old woman with symptomatic severe aortic stenosis and a small aortic annulus. Intraoperative evaluation revealed a 19-mm aortic annulus. After enlargement via a Y-incision and reconstruction with a bovine pericardial patch, a 23-mm mechanical prosthesis was successfully implanted without perioperative complications. Postoperative echocardiography demonstrated adequate prosthetic function, with a significant reduction in transvalvular gradients. Our initial experience suggests that the Yang technique is a safe, reproducible, and feasible option for centers introducing this procedure into their surgical practice. Although limited to a single case, the favorable outcome has encouraged our team to continue performing this technique in carefully selected patients.

title: Anesthetic Management of Pregnant Patients With Cardiovascular Disease: A Practical, Lesion-Based Clinical Review.
authors: Alexander Iosovich; Alexander Ronenson; Emilia Guasch; Nicolas Brogly; Yahya Aljuba; Daniel Shatalin
abstract: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is a major cause of maternal morbidity and mortality and increasingly complicates pregnancy as more women with congenital and acquired heart disease reach reproductive age. Anesthetic management of these patients requires integrating lesion-specific cardiovascular physiology, pregnancy-related hemodynamic changes, obstetric considerations, and the anticipated effects of labor, anesthesia, delivery, hemorrhage, and the postpartum transition. Despite contemporary cardiovascular and obstetric guidelines, translating lesion-specific physiology into practical anesthetic decisions remains challenging. This narrative review provides a practical framework for the peripartum anesthetic management of pregnant patients with CVD. We discuss contemporary risk assessment using the modified World Health Organization 2.0 classification and the Cardiac Disease in Pregnancy II risk model, followed by principles of Pregnancy Heart Team planning, labor analgesia, cesarean delivery, monitoring, anticoagulation, uterotonic therapy, and postpartum surveillance. Lesion-specific considerations are reviewed for mitral stenosis, aortic stenosis, aortic disease and coarctation, pulmonary hypertension, pregnancy-associated myocardial infarction, peripartum cardiomyopathy, congenital heart disease, and Fontan circulation. Particular attention is given to maintaining appropriate preload, ventricular filling, systemic vascular resistance, cardiac rhythm, and oxygenation while avoiding abrupt changes in vascular resistance or cardiac loading conditions. The review emphasizes individualized anesthetic planning rather than universal preferences for a particular anesthetic technique or mode of delivery. Neuraxial anesthesia can be advantageous in selected patients but should be considered in the context of ventricular function, pulmonary pressures, anticoagulation, urgency, and the expected hemodynamic response. General anesthesia remains an important option when neuraxial anesthesia is contraindicated or inadequate, rapid delivery is required, airway or ventilatory control is necessary, or maternal or surgical circumstances dictate. Uterotonic therapy should similarly be individualized according to cardiovascular physiology, with careful attention to dose, route, and hemodynamic effects. Close multidisciplinary planning and coordinated postpartum care are particularly important for women with pulmonary hypertension, ventricular dysfunction, complex congenital heart disease, and Fontan circulation.

title: Left Atrial Functional Parameters and Left Ventricular Reverse Remodeling After Aortic Valve Replacement in Severe Aortic Stenosis.
authors: Na Chen; Yongxin Li; Siqi Cao; Wenhui Gu; Huiyu Tang; Siyao Sun; Tao Cong; Haibo Wu; Jun Wu
abstract:
Left ventricular reverse remodeling (LVRR) after aortic valve replacement (AVR) varies in severe aortic stenosis (AS). We evaluated whether preoperative left atrial (LA)-derived functional indices were associated with structural LVRR (S-LVRR) and functional LVRR (F-LVRR).
This retrospective 2-center study included 139 adults with severe AS undergoing surgical or transcatheter AVR and follow-up echocardiography after a median of 6.1 months. S-LVRR was defined as normalization of left ventricular (LV) mass index, and F-LVRR as sex-specific recovery of absolute LV global longitudinal strain. Separate adjusted logistic models assessed LA reservoir strain (LASr), LA stiffness index (LASI), LA reservoir work, and LA volumetric/mechanical coupling index, with supportive sensitivity analyses.
S-LVRR and F-LVRR occurred in 58 (41.7%) and 42 (30.2%) patients, respectively. Higher LASr and lower LASI were independently associated with S-LVRR (odds ratio [OR] per 1-standard deviation increase, 2.48; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.37-4.49 and OR, 0.32; 95% CI, 0.13-0.79) and F-LVRR (OR, 7.41; 95% CI, 2.70-20.32 and OR, 0.01; 95% CI, 0.00-0.15). LASr remained robust across sensitivity analyses, whereas LASI was attenuated in change-based analyses.
In severe AS, preserved preoperative LASr and lower LASI were associated with postoperative LVRR after AVR. LASr was the most consistent LA-derived marker and may complement conventional LV assessment pending prospective validation.

title: The Art Behind the Algorithm: Hybrid Ablation and the Need for a Lifetime Strategy in Non-Paroxysmal Atrial Fibrillation.
authors: Cristiano Spadaccio; Stefano Schena; Andrew J Sherman
journal: Europace : European pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac electrophysiology : journal of the working groups on cardiac pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac cellular electrophysiology of the European Society of Cardiology
abstract: The management of persistent and long-standing persistent atrial fibrillation remains highly variable in clinical practice, despite increasingly refined guidelines and an expanding ablation armamentarium. Treatment sequencing is frequently driven by local program infrastructure and institutional culture, and hybrid ablation is often deferred until multiple endocardial procedures have failed, by which point progressive atrial remodeling may have already narrowed the therapeutic window. Randomized and registry data support a meaningful role for hybrid ablation earlier in the disease course of selected patients with non-paroxysmal AF, particularly those with enlarged atria, prolonged AF duration, advanced substrate, or failed prior endocardial ablation. Contemporary pulsed-field ablation technology has improved procedural safety and efficiency, yet freedom from recurrence at one year in persistent AF remains substantially lower than in paroxysmal AF across all current energy platforms, reflecting the complexity of atrial substrate over time. This ongoing myocardial remodeling places non-paroxysmal AF closer to a chronic structural cardiac disease than to a discrete procedural target and demands a lifetime management strategy rather than a sequence of isolated procedural decisions. The mindset for other progressive structural cardiac diseases has already moved in this direction-aortic valve stenosis is now managed through a multidisciplinary team that integrates anatomy, timing, procedural durability, and long-term risk across the full patient trajectory. We propose an AF Heart Team framework for non-paroxysmal AF in which catheter-based, hybrid, and surgical strategies are selected according to disease phenotype and lifetime trajectory, with the goal of intervening before advanced remodeling reduces the likelihood of durable rhythm control.

title: Variations in Access to Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation Versus Surgical Aortic Valve Replacement by Socioeconomic Factors: A Retrospective Population-Level Study in New South Wales, Australia.
authors: Md Shajedur Rahman Shawon; Jonathon B Ryan; Louisa Jorm
abstract:
Despite increasing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) activity in Australia in recent years, patient access to TAVI remains limited and is often more complex than access to surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR). The aim of this study was to identify socioeconomic factors associated with the likelihood of receiving TAVI versus SAVR in New South Wales (NSW), Australia.
Data from the NSW Admitted Patient Data Collection were used to compare the clinical and socioeconomic profiles of patients aged ≥65 years who underwent either TAVI or SAVR between 1 November 2017 and 28 February 2022. Multiple logistic regression analyses were performed on the overall patient cohort and on subgroups defined by age groups, hospital type and funding type.
The study included 6,493 patients (mean age: 79.1 years, 35.5% female) who underwent aortic valve replacement (SAVR=3,294; TAVI=3,199). The odds of receiving TAVI versus SAVR increased significantly with age (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] for patients aged 85 years and older versus those aged 75-84 years: 12.3, 95% CI: 9.99-15.2). Patients from the most disadvantaged socioeconomic areas had lower odds of receiving TAVI than those from the least disadvantaged areas (aOR:0.58, 95% CI: 0.47-0.73). Patients with private health insurance/Department of Veterans Affairs (PHI/DVA) funding were more likely to receive TAVI than SAVR (aOR: 3.29, 95% CI: 2.61-4.14), with this finding consistent across age groups and even more pronounced in patients treated in public hospitals (aOR: 5.82, 95% CI: 4.40-7.70).
Our study highlights significant variations in TAVI access based on age, socioeconomic status of area of residence, and funding type. These findings underscore the need for policy settings that promote equitable access and ensure that procedural choices for aortic valve replacement reflect clinical needs.

title: [Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting for Coronary Arteritis Induced by Myeloproliferative Neoplasms:Report of a Case].
authors: Zaiqiang Yu; Shuto Watanabe; Kenyu Murata; Yuki Imamura; Masahito Minakawa
journal: Kyobu geka. The Japanese journal of thoracic surgery
abstract: In a 60-year-old man with a history of stroke, coronary angiography revealed triple vessel disease, comprising left anterior descending artery (LAD) #6-7 with 99% diffuse stenosis within the stent, #11 and #12 with 90% stenosis, and right coronary artery (RCA) #1 stent with 50% stenosis. Cardiac ultrasonography showed 34% left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) without mitral regurgitation (MR) or tricuspid regurgitation (TR). Following median sternotomy, the bilateral internal thoracic artery (BITA) was harvested by skeletonization;however, dissection was confirmed at the distal end of the right internal thoracic artery (RITA). Owing to severe apical adhesions, we decided to perform on-pump beating coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) for this patient. Cardiopulmonary bypass was initiated via proximal aortic arch inflow and bicaval drainage without left ventricule (LV) venting. Subsequently, a left internal thoracic surgery (LITA)-free RITA composite Y-graft was prepared. On-pump beating CABG was performed in the graft design of the LITA-LAD (onlay patch, 4.5 cm), LITA-free RITA composite Y-graft to the obtuse marginal (OM) artery, and AO-saphenous vein graft (SVG)-4 posterior descending artery (PD)-4AV by sequential anastomosis. Many inflammatory cells invaded the RITA and coronary artery, and distal vessel thickening was confirmed but not in the ascending aorta. Coronary arteritis induced by myeloproliferative neoplasms was diagnosed based on pathology. Coronary computed tomography (CT) revealed the patency of all grafts.

title: [Non-anatomic Bypass for Severe Brachiocephalic Artery Stenosis due to Dissecting Aneurysm After Total Arch Aortic Replacement for Stanford Type A Acute Aortic Dissection:Report of a Case].
authors: Hana Fukuta; Ryohei Ushioda; Masahiko Narita; Yuki Setogawa; Hiroyuki Miyamoto; Ryo Okubo; Shogo Takahashi; Daisuke Takeyoshi; Shingo Kunioka; Masahiro Tsutsui; Hiroyuki Kamiya
journal: Kyobu geka. The Japanese journal of thoracic surgery
abstract: Dissecting brachiocephalic artery aneurysm after total arch aortic replacement poses a risk of postoperative cerebral infarction, yet no consensus exists regarding optimal management. Treatment decisions rely on the patient's condition, degree of true lumen stenosis, and lesion characteristics. We report a case of a dissecting brachiocephalic aneurysm with severe true lumen stenosis following surgery for Stanford type A acute aortic dissection. A 70-year-old man was transferred to our hospital with acute aortic dissection and multiple right-hemispheric cerebral infarctions and underwent emergency total arch replacement. On postoperative day nine, contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) revealed progressive false lumen expansion with significant true lumen compression. To prevent further cerebral ischemia, a left axillary-right common carotid artery non-anatomic bypass was performed. The patient gradually recovered left upper limb function and was transferred for rehabilitation on postoperative day 27.

title: Pearls & Oy-sters: Trace Visualization of the Central Retinal Artery: A Favorable Sign for Late-Window Endovascular Therapy in Central Retinal Artery Occlusion.
authors: Yang Du; Zhongqi Qi; Lu Cong; Dong Wang; Wanhu Liu; Shuo Zhang
abstract: In acute central retinal artery occlusion (CRAO), vessel stenosis and hemodynamic impairment significantly affect visual prognosis. We report a 69-year-old man who presented with 18 hours of acute, severe right eye blurred vision. Fundus examination and optical coherence tomography confirmed central retinal artery (CRA) occlusion with inner retinal edema. Digital subtraction angiography revealed an aortic arch variation and severe C1 segment stenosis of the right internal carotid artery (ICA), accompanied by delayed ophthalmic artery filling and faint visualization of the CRA. After multidisciplinary consultation, the patient underwent ICA stenting. Postoperative imaging showed resolved stenosis and improved retinal perfusion; the patient's vision subsequently improved and stabilized. This case suggests that revascularization can facilitate visual recovery even beyond the traditional window. Furthermore, faint CRA visualization on digital subtraction angiography indicates residual flow, providing a potential rationale for recanalization therapy.

title: Lipoprotein(a) in calcific aortic stenosis: mechanistic insights, clinical evidence, and emerging therapies.
authors: Wang Li; Shao Yun Shuang; You Bei An; Xu Yao; Wang Hao; Xu Xing Sheng; Pang Xue Lian; Meng Qing Feng
abstract: Calcific aortic stenosis (CAVS) is the most prevalent valvular heart disease affecting older adults, yet no validated pharmacological intervention can halt its progressive deterioration. Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] denotes a genetically regulated low-density lipoprotein (LDL)-like particle, in which apolipoprotein(a) forms a covalent bond with apolipoprotein B-100. Cumulative genetic, epidemiological, imaging and mechanistic research supports a causal role for elevated circulating Lp(a) in the initiation, and suggests a contribution to the advancement, of calcific aortic valve lesions. Lp(a) mediates valve injury mainly via preferentially transporting oxidized phospholipids (OxPL), anchoring within aortic valve leaflets, triggering endothelial activation and inflammatory cascades, as well as stimulating the autotaxin-lysophosphatidic acid (ATX-LPA) axis; collectively these signals drive osteogenic differentiation and mineralization of valve interstitial cells (VICs). Higher Lp(a) levels correlate with incident aortic valve calcification, accelerated hemodynamic deterioration, augmented calcium deposition quantified by computed tomography (CT), and elevated risks of aortic valve replacement (AVR) or all-cause cardiac death. Conventional lipid-lowering agents fail to reverse disease trajectory in patients with established CAVS. Though proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 (PCSK9) inhibitors only modestly cut Lp(a) concentrations, exploratory analyses have delivered preliminary suggestive signals for cardiovascular protection. RNA-targeted therapeutics and oral agents blocking Lp(a) assembly can reduce circulating Lp(a) by 70% up to over 95%, as demonstrated in early- and mid-phase clinical trials. Most notably, the ongoing Lp(a)FRONTIERS CAVS randomized trial is directly testing whether pelacarsen can decelerate CAVS progression, and no completed trial has yet demonstrated that Lp(a) lowering modifies CAVS disease. This narrative review summarizes Lp(a) biological characteristics, causal evidence linking Lp(a) to CAVS, together with opportunities and unresolved uncertainties surrounding Lp(a)-targeted therapeutic strategies.

title: Cardioplegia Strategies in Aortic Stenosis: A Focused Review of Current Evidence for Surgical Considerations.
authors: Minji Ho; Benjamin Chapman; Gianluca Lucchese; Paolo Bosco
abstract: Severe aortic stenosis (AS) exposes the hypertrophied myocardium to cardioplegic arrest in the setting of increased left ventricle (LV) mass, interstitial fibrosis, impaired relaxation, coronary microvascular dysfunction, and reduced perfusion reserve. These abnormalities may increase susceptibility to ischemic injury and complicate homogeneous cardioplegic delivery. This focused narrative review synthesizes physiological and clinical evidence on cardioplegia composition, temperature, delivery route, dosing, redosing, and myocardial protection during prolonged aortic cross-clamping in adults undergoing surgical aortic valve replacement. AS-specific comparative studies remain limited, generally small, and frequently reliant on biochemical markers; meanwhile, larger observational cohorts and contemporary randomized aortic valve replacement (AVR) trials also vary substantially in patient selection and myocardial protection protocols. Although some studies have associated cold blood cardioplegia with lower biomarker release than cold crystalloid cardioplegia, and cold maintenance strategies with less biochemical injury than warm cardioplegia, no formulation, temperature, or delivery route has demonstrated consistent superiority in clinically important outcomes. Limited historical evidence also suggests that body weight-based dosing may inadequately reflect myocardial requirements in marked LV hypertrophy, but no validated LV mass-based regimen currently exists. Therefore, cardioplegia in severe AS should be considered within a comprehensive myocardial protection protocol incorporating composition, temperature, dose, delivery route, redosing strategy, myocardial phenotype, associated valve or coronary disease, and anticipated cross-clamp duration. Prospective AS-specific studies using standardized protocols, LV mass stratification, and clinically meaningful outcomes are required.

title: Risk of Short-Term Stroke in Non-High-Risk Patients Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement vs Surgical Aortic Valve Replacement: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
authors: Haochen Liu; Zhidan Xiao; Jiahao Zou; Xiaoping Peng
abstract:
To compare the incidence of stroke at 1 and 2 years following transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) versus surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR), aiming to inform clinical decision-making regarding the safety and effectiveness of these interventions.
A random-effects meta-analysis was conducted including 9 randomized controlled trials (RCTs) with a total of 9865 patients. The primary endpoint was the incidence of stroke at 1 and 2 years post-procedure.
At 1 year, TAVR was associated with a lower incidence of stroke compared with SAVR (odds ratio (OR), 0.77; 95% confidence interval (CI), 0.61-0.98; p = 0.03). No significant difference was observed at 2 years (OR, 0.87; 95% CI, 0.65-1.17; p = 0.37).
TAVR significantly reduces the risk of stroke within 1 year post-procedure compared with SAVR; however, this effect was not maintained at 2 years. These findings highlight the early benefit of TAVR, while the long-term advantage requires further investigation.
This study has been registered with PROSPERO, registration number: CRD42025636191, https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD42025636191.

title: Experimental study of TPU and SEBS additively manufactured leaflets for novel aortic valve polymer TAVI prosthesis.
authors: Alex G Kuchumov; Denis Khoroshev; Aleksandra Kutuzova; Aleksei Baranov; Oleg Krestyaninov; Ekaterina Barbashina; Pavel Zelenchuk; Edward Matjeka; Thanyani Pandelani; Fulufhelo Nemavhola
abstract:
Transcatheter valve implantation is a cutting-edge technology for high and low risk patients with aortic stenosis. Bioprosthetic valves are limited due to several disadvantages as a long-term durability and structural valve degeneration. Polymeric aortic valve leaflet devices represent state-of-the-art technology to overcome limitations of bioprostheses. Nevertheless, more recent biocompatible and biostable polymers have revealed a significant potential. Additionally, 3D additive manufacturing opens new paths for patient-specific design of biomedical implants. Flexible polymers may not only mimic native aortic valve, but also may improve long-term durability. Polyurethanes and styrene polymers are promising materials for modern polymer valves. Nevertheless, mechanical properties of additive manufactured TPU or SEBS leaflets are not properly studied.
Experimental study of TPU and SEBS samples and aortic valve leaflets for novel aortic valve polymer TAVI prosthesis is presented. Tensile tests and compression tests of three types of FDM-printed samples with various filament alignments (axial alignment, transversal alignment, diagonal alignment) were performed. The results of tests confirmed that longitudinal axial alignment achieve a maximum stress compared to transversal and diagonal directions. Compressive tests of TPU and SEBS 3D-manufactured aortic valve leaflets with digital image correlation technology were performed. Young's modulus and Poisson's ratio were evaluated. Moreover, parameters of constitutive models were found.
The TPU tensile specimen exhibits the highest stress/strain values at a speed of 100 mm/min, regardless of the filament alignment pattern. Slightly lower results are observed at a speed of 50 mm/min, which is likely associated with a wide range of plastic deformation. In the case of SEBS, a different pattern is observed: at 500 mm/min, it demonstrates high resistance to fracture, unlike TPU. A comparison of TPU and SEBS specimens at the same speeds and with the same alignment, based on maximum stress values, shows a minimal difference of 4% with the axial alignment at a speed of 50 mm/min; however, when comparing strains, the difference increases to 90%. The results of the compression experiment on aortic valve specimens made of TPU and SEBS at a speed of 30 mm/min showed that TPU force values for is considerably lower (4% of the maximum case), while for SEBS the spread increases to 20% of the maximum case.
SEBS aortic valve leaflets were shown to be stiffer than TPU. It can be a step for choice of stiffer/softer leaflets for patient-specific device. The proposed approach can help manufacturers in elaboration and manufacturing of new TAVI polymer devices design made of TPU and SEBS polymers for clinical applications.

title: Deep Learning-Based Analysis of Microscopic Hyperspectral Images of HER2-Stained Breast Cancer Sections for Molecular Status Prediction.
authors: Lin Yan; Yan Wan; Haonan Liu; Wenlou Liu; Yang Zhao; Hongmei Wang; Juanjuan Tang; Xuanyu Chen; Zhengxiang Han; Xiaobing Qin
abstract: HER2 assessment in breast cancer relies on immunohistochemistry (IHC) with reflex in situ hybridization for equivocal cases, while conventional bright-field imaging provides limited quantitative optical information. We investigated microscopic hyperspectral imaging (HSI) of HER2-stained sections for slide-level molecular status prediction. HSI data from 43 cases (21 HER2-positive, 22 HER2-negative; 400-1000 nm, 128 bands) were acquired between January 2024 and August 2025. After calibration, optical-density conversion, tissue masking, and Savitzky-Golay smoothing, we developed SpectralMix-MIL, a weakly supervised multiple-instance learning model combining learnable spectral projection (K = 32) with attention pooling. On a patient-level 7:3 train/test split, SpectralMix-MIL achieved an AUROC of 0.923 and AUPRC of 0.910. Repeated stratified fivefold cross-validation yielded mean AUROC 0.904 ± 0.041 and AUPRC 0.892 ± 0.045, while leave-one-out cross-validation yielded AUROC 0.897. These findings support microscopic HSI for quantitative breast cancer molecular phenotyping, pending larger external validation.

title: Bacterial protein function prediction via multimodal deep learning.
authors: Lukas Miklautz; Leyden Fernandez; Giulia Muzio; Michael Adamer; Karsten Borgwardt; Kemal Avican
abstract: Bacterial proteins are specialized with extensive functional diversity for survival in diverse and stressful environments. A significant portion of these proteins remains functionally uncharacterized, limiting our understanding of bacterial survival mechanisms. Hence, we develop Deep Expression STructure (DeepEST), a multimodal deep learning framework that predicts protein function in bacteria by assigning Gene Ontology (GO) terms. DeepEST comprises two modules: a multi-layer perceptron that uses gene expression and gene location, and a protein structure-based module that uses predicted structures and amino acid sequences. Within DeepEST, we integrate these modules through a learnable weighted linear combination and introduce a novel masked loss function to fine-tune the structure-based predictor for bacterial species. These choices are well suited for bacteria, in which functionally related genes frequently colocalize and are cotranscribed within operons, allowing transcription dynamics to serve as informative, condition-dependent signals. We show that DeepEST outperforms existing protein function prediction methods on a 25-species benchmark, relying solely on amino acid sequence or protein structure. Averaged over the 25 species, DeepEST reaches a protein-centric F max of 0.689 and a term-centric micro-AUPRC of 0.756, a relative improvement of 4.4% and 11.6% over the second-best method, the structure-based predictor DeepFRI. Moreover, DeepEST predicts GO terms for unclassified hypothetical proteins across 25 human bacterial pathogens, supporting their experimental characterization. DeepEST bridges organism-specific data integration and structure-based transfer learning, providing a method tailored for bacterial protein function prediction in settings with structural and multi-condition expression data.

title: Artificial intelligence in temporomandibular disorders: A bibliometric analysis of research trends, hotspots, and emerging frontiers.
authors: Xuhui Fan; Xixin Gao; Shuning Li
abstract:
Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly applied to temporomandibular disorders (TMD), particularly in imaging, diagnosis, classification, and prediction. However, the global research landscape, knowledge structure, and evolving research priorities remain insufficiently characterized. This study aimed to systematically map the development and emerging trends of AI research in TMD.
A total of 311 publications from 2015 to 2026 were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection. Bibliometric and visualization analyses were conducted using CiteSpace, VOSviewer, and R (bibliometrix) to examine publication trends, scientific collaboration, citation networks, research hotspots, and thematic evolution.
Publication output increased markedly after 2019, reaching its highest level in 2025. China contributed the most publications (n = 111), followed by the United States (n = 70), South Korea (n = 45), and Turkey (n = 33), with differences in international collaboration patterns. The knowledge structure reflected interdisciplinary connections among dentistry, medical imaging, computer science, and engineering. Major research hotspots included machine learning, deep learning, magnetic resonance imaging, automated diagnosis, disease classification, and prediction. Temporal analyses revealed a shift from algorithm development toward imaging-based assessment, TMD classification, and clinically oriented predictive applications.
AI-related TMD research has expanded rapidly, with increasing emphasis on diagnostic and predictive applications. Future research should prioritize standardized protocols, multicenter datasets, external validation, and evaluation of clinical applicability to facilitate reliable integration into TMD management.

title: A 3D Deep Learning Model for Assessing Concomitant Pulmonary Embolism Risk by Integrating Clinical and Computed Tomography Venography Features in Patients with Lower Extremity Deep Venous Thrombosis.
authors: Yue Zhang; Zhi-Wei Zhang; Xing-Tao Huang; Zhi-Chuan Zhang; Yi-Bo Feng; Tian-You Luo; Fa-Jin Lv; Qi Li
journal: European journal of vascular and endovascular surgery : the official journal of the European Society for Vascular Surgery
abstract:
The aim of this study was to develop and validate a multimodal deep learning (DL) model integrating clinical and computed tomography venography (CTV) features for predicting concomitant acute pulmonary embolism (PE) risk in patients with lower extremity deep venous thrombosis (LEDVT).
This multicentre retrospective study enrolled patients with LEDVT undergoing both computed tomography pulmonary angiography and lower extremity CTV. Centre 1 data were used for model training and internal validation, while data from centres 2 and 3 were used for external testing. Clinical models (logistic regression [LR], random forest [RF], support vector machine [SVM], and XGBoost), 3D DL models (VGG-11, VGG-16, ResNet-18, Res2Net-50, and DenseNet-121), and combined models (LR, RF, SVM, and XGBoost) integrating clinical, imaging, and DL features were developed to select the best performer, which was further benchmarked against validated clinical risk scores (Wells score and modified Geneva score).
A total of 348 patients from centre 1 were randomly split into training and internal validation sets, and 127 patients from two independent institutions formed the external testing cohort. The optimal LR clinical, 3D VGG-16 DL, and SVM combined models achieved external testing area under the curve (AUC) values of 0.776, 0.789, and 0.836, respectively. DeLong tests confirmed that the SVM combined model significantly outperformed the LR clinical model and validated clinical scores (all p < .050) on the external testing set, while yielding a comparable AUC to the 3D VGG-16 DL model. Decision curve analysis indicated higher net benefit for the SVM combined model, alongside superior calibration, and positive net reclassification improvement and integrated discrimination improvement values.
The SVM combined model integrating clinical, imaging, and DL features demonstrated robust performance, offering a promising tool for predicting concomitant acute PE in patients with LEDVT.

title: MONKEY Challenge: Machine-learning for Optimal detection of iNflammatory cells in KidnEY transplant biopsies.
authors: Dominique van Midden; Fazael Ayatollahi; Miriam Immink; Jesper Kers; Eric J Steenbergen; Jiaqi Lv; Esha Sadia Nasir; Kesi Xu; Shan E Ahmed Raza; Thibaut Goldsborough; Peter Bankhead; Gunjan Deotale; Abhishek Ambast; Lavish Ramchandani; Dev Kumar Das; Tri Q Nguyen; Nicolas Kozakowski; Maximilian C Koeller; Mark D Stegall; Walter D Park; José Antonio Rodriguez Calero; Alton Brad Farris; MONKEY consortium; Luuk B Hilbrands; Jeroen A W M van der Laak; Linda Studer
journal: Laboratory investigation; a journal of technical methods and pathology
abstract:
Accurate quantification of inflammatory cells in Periodic Acid-Schiff (PAS)-stained kidney transplant biopsies is essential for Banff classification but remains subjective and labor-intensive. To address this, the MONKEY challenge benchmarked deep learning (DL) methods for automated detection of mononuclear leukocytes and their subtypes.
A multicenter dataset of 118 biopsies with co-registered PAS and immunohistochemically restained slides, comprising over 131,000 annotated cells, was used. The algorithms were evaluated on hold-out validation and test set using Free-response Receiver Operating Characteristic (FROC) analysis, alongside precision, recall, and F1-scores.
Across diverse architectures, performance converged, with the top models achieving F1-scores up to 0.75 for overall detection. Lymphocyte detection performed well (F1 up to 0.78), whereas monocyte detection remained more challenging (F1 up to 0.47). To explore the potential clinical applicability of automated inflammatory cell detection, the winning model was integrated with renal tissue segmentation models, enabling compartment-specific evaluation and quantitative assessment of Banff-related lesions. In an independent multicenter cohort of 180 kidney transplant biopsies, DL-derived quantitative measurements demonstrated strong correlations with consensus pathologist scoring for several inflammation-related Banff lesions, particularly total inflammation and interstitial inflammation.
This study establishes the first multicenter, PAS-based, IHC-validated benchmark for inflammatory cell detection and provides a clinically grounded resource to support the development of robust, generalizable AI systems for transplant pathology. Beyond benchmark performance, our extended tissue-specific analyses demonstrate that inflammatory cell detection on routine PAS slides can be anatomically contextualized and translated into quantitative measurements that align with conventional Banff lesion assessment, providing a foundation for future AI-assisted evaluation of kidney transplant biopsies.

title: A Systematic Review of Bias, Validation, and Explainability in Artificial Intelligence Algorithms for Dental Diagnostics.
authors: Adel Alrayes; Dimitrios Kollias; Aylin Baysan
abstract:
To critically evaluate the current role of artificial intelligence (AI) in dental diagnosis across multiple dental disciplines, assessing diagnostic performance, methodological quality, risk of bias, validation, explainability, and clinical applicability.
This systematic review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA guidelines and registered in PROSPERO (CRD42025639340). PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Embase, LILACS, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, Web of Science, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched up to December-2025. Two reviewers independently performed study selection, data extraction, and risk-of-bias assessment. Risk of bias in diagnostic accuracy studies was assessed using QUADAS-2-tool, evaluating the domains of patient selection, index test, reference standard, flow and timing whilst randomised studies were assessed using Cochrane RoB 2-tool. Reporting quality and transparency of AI-model development and validation were assessed using the selected items from TRIPOD-AI reporting guideline. Methodological quality and risk of bias in AI model development and evaluation were additionally assessed using PROBAST+AI.
Ninety-six studies met the inclusion criteria, of which 90.6% were retrospective. Convolutional neural networks (CNN) were the most frequently used architecture (82.3%). Sixteen studies failed to specify the CNN architecture used. Reported diagnostic accuracy ranged from 81% to 99% across dental specialties, with high performance in implantology (92-99%), orthodontics (88-99%), endodontics (87-99%). Panoramic radiographs and cone-beam computed tomography were the most used imaging modalities. QUADAS-2 analysis indicated that high-risk of bias in 55.2% of studies and most lacked external validation, whilst Assessment using selected TRIPOD+AI items identified important gaps in reporting completeness and transparency, particularly in sample-size justification, missing-data handling, protocol availability, study registration, and data or code availability.
AI demonstrates substantial technical capability to enhance diagnostic accuracy and efficiency. However, the predominance of retrospective designs, limited external validation, and methodological weaknesses constrain the strength of current evidence.
The use of AI is potentially considered as a decision-support tool rather than replacement for clinical judgement.

title: Bridging HRMS spectra and anti-Staphylococcus aureus activity by machine learning for prioritization of putative antibacterial contaminants in wastewater.
authors: Shuyang Feng; Shuran Li; Xiaoping Shi; Ming Ying; Minxin Ji; Jingya Lou; Xu Yan; Gang Wu; Xu-Xiang Zhang
abstract: Antibacterial contaminants are an increasing environmental and public health concern, yet prioritizing compounds with potential antibacterial activity in wastewater remains challenging. We developed machine learning models linking MS/MS-derived probabilistic fingerprints to activity against Staphylococcus aureus, enabling activity-guided prioritization before structural elucidation. Among 36 machine learning and deep learning configurations across different algorithms and fingerprint representations, MLP_PubChem and XGBoost_PubChem achieved the highest observed test F1 scores in positive- and negative-ion modes, respectively (0.48 and 0.42; AUROC, 0.84 for both). SHAP analysis examined feature contributions in positive-ion RF_Both and negative-ion XGBoost_PubChem. For wastewater screening, positive-ion MLP_Both (test F1, 0.475; AUROC, 0.847) and negative-ion XGBoost_PubChem prioritized 89 of 3797 successfully scored features, reducing the immediate follow-up list by 97.66%. Database searches yielded 39 candidate annotations for structural investigation. Retrospective screening identified MS/MS matches to prioritized candidate features in public wastewater datasets from multiple geographical regions. A web application is available at https://huggingface.co/spaces/dgfhdu/P-A to support candidate screening. By focusing structural elucidation on features with predicted anti-S. aureus activity, this workflow supports non-targeted screening guided by biological activity.

title: A novel deep learning-based peak detection technique for in vivo metabolite analysis of triterpenoids from Eleutherococcus senticosus leaves in Parkinson's disease mice.
authors: Tiantian Wen; Wei Guan; Shiqi Xu; Xu Yang; Yanying Li; Hao Wang; Peng Jiang; Qingshan Chen; Lili Zhang; Quanyong Wang; Haixue Kuang; Shu Liu; Yan Liu
abstract: To address the challenges in mass spectrometry data processing, including poor detection of low-abundance metabolites, severe noise interference, and the reliance on labor-intensive parameter tuning in conventional peak detection methods, a deep learning-based peak detection algorithm termed MSPeakNet was developed. The model used a multi-scale convolutional module and a U-net encoder-decoder architecture integrated with an attention mechanism, enabling high-precision peak identification and noise reduction in complex biological matrices. MSPeakNet achieved precision and F1 scores comparable to CWT, with superior noise robustness, while maintaining competitive recall. The developed method was subsequently applied to the in vivo metabolite profiling of total triterpenoids from Eleutherococcus senticosus leaves (ESLT) in an MPTP-induced mouse model of Parkinson's disease (PD) using UPLC-Q-TOF/MS analysis. A total of 143 ESLT-related compounds, comprising 88 prototypes and 55 metabolites, were identified in plasma, urine, feces, and brain tissue, of which 16 prototypes were detected in brain tissue. Pharmacodynamic evaluation further confirmed that ESLT significantly ameliorated MPTP-induced motor dysfunction and dopaminergic neuronal loss. Comparative analysis further revealed distinct profiles of ESLT-related differential compounds between PD model and normal mice across multiple biological matrices; 14, 9, 6, and 4 differential metabolites were identified in feces, urine, plasma, and brain, respectively, suggesting that disease status may affect the biotransformation, distribution, and elimination of ESLT constituents. A robust and efficient deep learning-based approach for mass spectrometry peak detection was thereby established, and critical experimental evidence was provided for the discovery of anti-Parkinsonian active ingredients and quality markers from E. senticosus leaves.

title: Temporal regularization of a dynamic graph network for ordinal prediction of discharge disposition after ischemic stroke in intensive care.
authors: Luning Wang; Zhipeng Wang; Changsong Wang; Pengli Zhai; Hui Feng; Hongmei Liu; Qian Hou; Ming Guo
abstract:
Early identification of poor outcome after acute ischemic stroke is difficult. Electronic health record models often discard the physiological trajectory; whether a biological prior improves prediction is unclear.
We studied 5,101 MIMIC-IV admissions with cerebral infarction, ICD-10 I63; 2,874 had a usable intensive care time series, a mapped outcome and static features at a 24 h landmark. The outcome was discharge disposition on a six-level scale, every predictor restricted to the first 24 h. A dynamic graph recurrent network applied a monotone-progress, bounded-drift penalty to its trajectory score, tested against a matched generic smoothness penalty and two negative controls under patient-grouped cross-validation.
At the 24 h landmark the gradient-boosted model with time-series summaries reached a macro-AUC of 0.743, 95% CI 0.733 to 0.753. The nested stacking ensemble reached 0.750, 0.739 to 0.760, a difference compatible with zero; it was not transported externally. Reversing or time-permuting the penalty, or substituting a smoothness penalty, left the macro-AUC within 0.002; no pathway information enters the loss. The transported gradient-boosted model reached 0.809 in eICU-CRD and 0.814 in MIMIC-III. A second, harmonized-schema ensemble reached 0.844 in eICU-CRD, 0.029 above its strongest component, but that gain did not carry to MIMIC-III.
Discharge disposition after ischemic stroke is partly predictable from the first 24 h of intensive care data, and no ensemble gain was established. The penalty is a generic smoothness constraint motivated by, not derived from, transcriptomic observations. The endpoint is care placement, not functional recovery.

title: A multi-scale attention multi-task 1D-CNN for predicting rice chemical components at different milling degrees using hyperspectral imaging.
authors: Ze Sun; Mengyuan Wang; Hao Li; Anqi Li; Yanlong Han; Haonan Gao; Tianyi Wang
abstract: Precise quantification of nutritional components in rice is crucial for achieving moderate milling. However, traditional detection methods often struggle to simultaneously meet the demands for efficient, non-destructive and multi-indicator analysis. To predict the chemical components of rice at different milling degrees, this study utilized a fusion of hyperspectral imaging and deep learning. The results demonstrated that the multi-task 1D-CNN with a multi-scale attention mechanism outperformed traditional regression models. The coefficient of determination and residual predictive deviation for cellulose, fat and protein exceeded 0.92 and 3.65, respectively. Additionally, the root mean square error and mean absolute error were below 0.16 and 0.13, respectively. The results introduce an innovative approach to food inspection and provide insights into the chemical variations associated with grain refinement.

title: Physics-constrained pairwise representation learning for Raman spectra matching.
authors: Haohao Sun; Xiaolong Zou; Yilong Zhang; Haixia Wang; Ronghua Liang; Peng Chen
journal: Spectrochimica acta. Part A, Molecular and biomolecular spectroscopy
abstract: Raman spectroscopy is a powerful and reliable tool for analyzing the chemical information of substances. Practical Raman spectra are often degraded by fluorescence background, stray light, environmental noise, and acquisition variations, leading to peak distortion, baseline drift, and reduced spectral consistency, which significantly increase the difficulty of reliable spectral matching. Existing deep learning methods have demonstrated promising performance by automatically learning spectral representations. Nevertheless, most of them are designed for classification tasks, making the learned features insufficiently robust to spectral degradation and diverse real-world Raman acquisition conditions. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a Physics-constrained Multi-Scale Network for Raman Spectroscopy (PCMS-Net) for robust spectral matching. A spectral simulation strategy based on physical guidance was developed to generate degradation-aware training pairs with diverse but physically reasonable spectral variations. Based on the Siamese matching framework, PCMS-Net directly learns the spectral similarity feature representations. PCMS-Net maintains the physical consistency of spectral features during the degradation process, constrains the feature representations, and simultaneously captures global spectral semantics and local multi-scale peak details to enhance the feature representations. This design enables the network to learn feature representations with discrimination and robustness for spectral matching. Experimental results show that PCMS-Net consistently outperforms traditional and representative deep learning methods in Raman spectral matching, demonstrating strong robustness under diverse real-world acquisition conditions.

title: Single prior-based 3D volumetric tracking from a planar snapshot in spine SBRT: A proof-of-concept study.
authors: Euidam Kim; Donghyeok Choi; Yoonsun Chung; Hugh Lee
journal: Physica medica : PM : an international journal devoted to the applications of physics to medicine and biology : official journal of the Italian Association of Biomedical Physics (AIFB)
abstract:
Continuous 3D onboard monitoring is essential to ensure accurate dose delivery of stereotactic body radiation therapy. However, current approaches for 2D-to-3D volumetric estimation typically require extensive patient-specific data, or depend on auxiliary imaging hardware. This study introduces a proof-of-concept framework for data-efficient, patient-specific 3D volumetric tracking using only a single volumetric prior.
A retrospective dataset of 80 spine SBRT patients was utilized. Digitally Reconstructed Radiographs synthesized from cone-beam computed tomography volumes served as surrogates for onboard kV projections. The pipeline consists of patient-agnostic pre-training using an archival dataset, patient-specific adaptation using the single volumetric prior supplemented by non-rigid motion simulations, and simulated intra-fractional 3D estimation. The network employs a modified Attention U-Net with a channel-to-depth bottleneck and a triple feature concatenation to map the 2D to 3D spatial domain.
The proposed model demonstrated a statistically significant improvement in structural tracking capabilities compared to a static uncompensated baseline. Furthermore, the performance variance across patients was substantially compressed, enhancing reliability against setup uncertainties while achieving high spatial concordance in the complex spinal anatomy. The inference throughput reached approximately 10 frames per second.
This proof-of-concept study establishes the technical feasibility of data-efficient, patient-specific onboard volumetric tracking using a single volumetric prior by successfully resolving anatomical deformations from a single 2D projection in near real-time.

title: A deep monitoring microfluidic platform for label-free identification and nanodrug evaluation in lung cancer.
authors: Shuaishuai Zhang; Bing Bo; Haiyan Gu; Mingcan Chen; Dihang Wu; Yingchuan Li; Jixiang Wang; Jingjing Xu
abstract: Real-time detection of rare cancer cells holds potential for guiding more informed treatment decisions at the bedside. However, conventional enrichment methods are limited by low sensitivity, a high risk of cell damage, and prolonged processing times. To address these challenges, this study developed an intelligent micro-total analysis platform toward H1299 cells (a metastatic non-small cell lung cancer cell line). The system integrates a cascaded dual-microfluidic chip architecture with a high-resolution microscope driven by a deep learning-based detection framework. Finite element simulations were performed to optimize droplet generation conditions for the cross-junction microfluidic chip. A dataset of 749 high-resolution droplet images (1536 × 1024 pixels) was constructed, comprising 2619 live H1299 lung cancer cells distributed across 5127 droplets. Among the algorithms evaluated, the YOLOv7 model was selected and optimized, achieving a detection accuracy above 98% and a real-time inference speed exceeding 55 frames per second. As a proof of concept, the platform was applied to quantitatively analyze single-cell level responses to anticancer drugs in undiluted whole blood and processed biopsy samples within 30-40 min, yielding results consistent with those of the standard Cell Counting Kit-8 (CCK-8) assay. The minimal sample requirement, label-free operation, and stable performance of the system underscore its potential for treatment monitoring. Moreover, its capacity for continuous image acquisition and autonomous analysis may facilitate dynamic monitoring in future cancer research.

title: HMVPS-DRP: Hybrid multi-view representation learning and pathway-state-aware graph learning for interpretable cancer drug response prediction with multi-omics data.
authors: Wei Wang; Di Wang; Biao Li; Yun Zhou
abstract: Cancer drug response prediction is an important task in precision oncology and can support personalized treatment and candidate anticancer drug screening. Although many deep learning methods have been developed, existing approaches still do not fully exploit complementary information from different molecular views of drugs. Meanwhile, multi-omics data are often processed by independent encoders or simple fusion strategies, which limits the characterization of cell line molecular states. In addition, jointly modeling pathway structural priors and cell-line-specific pathway activity remains challenging. To address these limitations, we propose HMVPS-DRP, an interpretable multi-omics framework that integrates hybrid multi-view representation learning with pathway-state-aware graph learning. HMVPS-DRP first jointly learns molecular graph topology, SMILES sequence semantics, and substructure information from ECFP fingerprints to obtain complementary and comprehensive drug representations. Meanwhile, pathway connections based on gene-set overlap and cell-line-specific pathway activity states are integrated into pathway-cell line heterogeneous graphs, allowing the model to combine pathway structural information with cell-line-specific functional states. We further design a condition aware aggregation module that uses multi-omics data to regulate pathway information propagation and attention based feature aggregation, thereby enhancing cell line representation learning. Comprehensive experiments on the GDSC and PRISM datasets demonstrate the predictive performance of HMVPS-DRP. On the primary GDSC dataset, HMVPS-DRP achieves an RMSE of 0.9410, a PCC of 0.9364, and an SCC of 0.9165. Pathway and gene attribution analyses provide molecular-level interpretations of model predictions, while a melanoma case study highlights the potential of HMVPS-DRP to predict drug responses and support candidate anticancer drug screening.

title: Rethinking neural network reparameterized full waveform inversion: A Hessian perspective.
authors: Peng Jiang; Sihan Chen; Yuxiao Ren; Senlin Yang; Bin Liu
journal: Neural networks : the official journal of the International Neural Network Society
abstract: By seamlessly integrating deep neural networks (DNNs) into the traditional full waveform inversion (FWI) framework, the neural-network-reparameterized FWI (RFWI) naturally introduces implicit regularization, thereby mitigating key challenges in practical applications-such as sensitivity to initial models and susceptibility to local minima. While a variety of advanced RFWI methods have been proposed to enhance inversion performance, profound insights remain lacking in two key questions: (1) How does the DNN improve the robustness of RFWI, (2) How to further improve the performance of RFWI. In response to the first question, the Hessian spectrum is introduced as an analytical tool to reveal the difference in optimization characteristics between RFWI and traditional FWI. Our findings demonstrate that the superior robustness arises from the persistent constraints imposed by DNN on the inversion process, guiding a long-lasting tendency towards the eigenvectors associated with large eigenvalues, which correspond to stable directions dominated by low-frequency information. For the second question, we propose two improvement techniques based on the inherent optimization characteristics of RFWI, targeting convergence or robustness, both of which have the potential to generalize to other RFWI implementations. Focusing on convergence improvement in ideal scenarios, we propose the Adam+L-BFGS hybrid optimizer, which accelerates high-frequency fitting while avoiding local minima. Regarding robustness improvement in challenging scenarios, we propose a Hessian trace-based regularization technique that promotes flatter optimization trajectories, thereby mitigating the overfitting of noise. The experimental results support the effectiveness of our proposed improvement techniques.

title: Monotonicity constraints in neural networks: A survey and future directions.
authors: Junpeng Sun; Juan Luis Suárez; Weiping Ding; Salvador García
journal: Neural networks : the official journal of the International Neural Network Society
abstract: Monotonicity constraints are important in many machine learning applications where domain knowledge indicates that predictions should follow monotonic relationships with respect to certain input features. Incorporating monotonicity constraints into neural networks has attracted increasing attention. However, existing neural networks differ significantly in how they implement monotonicity and lack a systematic analysis of monotonicity design. This paper provides a comprehensive study of monotonicity constraints in neural networks. First, we formalize monotonicity and clarify its relationship to related concepts. Based on this, we propose a unified taxonomy that organizes existing methods into two categories: structure-based monotonicity approaches, which guarantee monotonicity through architectural design and parameter constraints, and non-structural monotonicity approaches, which induce, verify, or certify monotonicity without encoding it directly into the architecture. Second, we conduct a systematic empirical comparison of representative methods across 12 real-world tabular datasets using a unified evaluation protocol. The results show that carefully designed structure-based approaches can achieve predictive performance comparable to unconstrained neural networks while guaranteeing monotonic behavior, whereas naive constraint implementations often suffer from limited expressive capacity. Non-structural approaches provide greater flexibility and can adapt to existing architectures, but their effectiveness and guarantee strength depend strongly on the specific mechanism. Overall, this work offers a unified perspective on designing monotonicity constraints in neural networks. The source code and datasets are available at https://github.com/junpeng-sun/MonNN.

title: STMH-Xception: Sequential multi-head residual learning for robust underwater acoustic target recognition.
authors: Chenhong Yan; Shefeng Yan; Ruobin Gao; Yang Yu; Guang Pan; Jinpeng Xu; Ponnuthurai N Suganthan
journal: Neural networks : the official journal of the International Neural Network Society
abstract: Underwater Acoustic Target Recognition (UATR) remains a formidable challenge due to highly non-stationary marine environments and the complex, overlapping acoustic signatures of different vessels. Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) typically employ a single-head optimization paradigm, rendering them susceptible to overfitting individual-vessel noise rather than learning robust, category-consistent features. To bridge this gap, we propose a novel framework, the Sequentially Trained Multi-Head Xception (STMH-Xception). Drawing inspiration from gradient boosting, we introduce a step-wise STMH strategy that integrates deeply supervised auxiliary heads into a depthwise separable convolutional backbone. Unlike standard joint-training multi-task learning, STMH employs a sequential freezing protocol whereby each subsequent head targets and corrects the residual representation errors of its predecessors. This "coarse-to-fine" learning scheme drives the network to extract a highly discriminative feature hierarchy while mitigating inter-head gradient conflicts associated with joint multi-head optimization. Validated on the ShipsEar and DeepShip datasets, the proposed STMH-Xception increases the classification accuracy from 68.72% to 73.10% and from 72.89% to 76.14%, respectively, compared to the baseline. Supported by statistical significance tests and generalizability analyses across diverse CNN encoders, the STMH strategy emerges as a highly efficient, CNN-backbone-agnostic optimization paradigm. The additional parameter and computational cost introduced by the auxiliary heads remain small, making the framework promising for resource-constrained UATR scenarios.

title: DeCITS: Incomplete time series clustering with deep contrastive learning.
authors: Ying Zhong; Haiyan Wang; Dong Huang; Yuan-Kun Xu; Chang-Dong Wang; Huiru Zhou
journal: Neural networks : the official journal of the International Neural Network Society
abstract: Time series data often contains missing values in real-world applications, making incomplete time series clustering a significant research focus in recent years. However, incorporating imputation and clustering within a model can lead to rapid error propagation from imputed values. Many existing time series clustering methods struggle to reduce the error propagation from imputation to clustering. Additionally, how to learn cluster-friendly representations from unlabeled time series data with temporal dynamics, and how to isolate the representation extracted from the clustering task without considering their interaction, remain challenging issues. In light of this, this study presents a Deep Contrastive Incomplete Time Series Clustering (DeCITS) method, which utilizes a unified framework for learning representations of incomplete time series in a contrastive learning manner. To mitigate error propagation, an adversarial strategy is incorporated to distinguish real and imputed values, encouraging the model to impute more realistic missing data. Consequently, DeCITS obtains cluster-friendly representations and achieves highly competitive clustering performance. Extensive experiments on six real-world datasets and eight UCR datasets demonstrate the superiority of DeCITS over existing state-of-the-art methods.

abstract: Introduction: Height, weight, and age of person has significant impact on the normal size of heart. title: Understanding pedagogical challenges faced by technology teachers in special needs classrooms
authors: Katane Elizabeth Kekana; Thokozani Isaac Mtshali
journal: Journal of Education and Learning Technology
abstract: Teaching learners with special educational needs requires dynamic and adaptive pedagogical strategies that can lead to social development and academic success. This can be possible if teachers are assisted in mitigating the daily challenges of teaching such learners. This qualitative exploratory case study investigated the pedagogical challenges encountered by two Grade 9 Technology teachers in the Capricorn District of Limpopo Province. This study used Shulman’s Content and Pedagogical Knowledge framework to understand teachers’ challenges. Data was collected through semi-structured interviews and classroom observations; all collected data were analysed thematically. This study found that teachers experienced various challenges, including the emotional labour of teaching, burnout in the LSEN environment and the enactment of instructional knowledge. The study concluded that the sampled teachers displayed weaknesses in lesson planning, activating learners’ prior knowledge, diagnosing errors, achieving curriculum objectives and sustaining engagement. As a result, it was recommended that support through teacher assistants, creative differentiated strategies and enhanced digital-technology literacy to improve outcomes for learners with special needs was imminent.
