title: Integration of Biomechanics and Digital Technology: Using Kinovea for Motion Analysis and Learning for Beginner Athletes
authors: Muhammad Nur Hudha; Riezky Maya Probosari; Annisa Nur Khasanah; Supurwoko; Salsabila Kholifahtun Nisa’; Gifran Rihla Gifarka Latief
journal: Journal of Coaching and Sports Science
abstract: Background: The integration of biomechanics with digital motion-analysis technologies has introduced new approaches for examining movement efficiency, kinematic characteristics, and technical patterns in walking and running activities. Kinovea, as an accessible motion-analysis software, provides both visual and quantitative feedback. However, its application in supporting technique development among beginner athletes remains insufficiently explored. Aim: This study aims to describe the use of Kinovea in biomechanics training and examine its contribution to the awareness of kinematic characteristics and movement techniques among beginner athletes. Methods: A descriptive qualitative design involved 72 beginner athletes aged 18–25 years selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected over 16 weeks through interviews, field observations, and motion video recordings analyzed using Kinovea. Kinematic data focused on joint angles, stride behavior, and movement phases during walking, running, and the flight phase. Qualitative data were analyzed using content analysis with NVivo 12, while kinematic results were interpreted descriptively to identify performance patterns and areas for technical refinement. Result: Kinematic analysis showed coordinated joint-angle patterns across all phases. Walking analysis identified arm swing angles of 50.9°–58.8° and leg separation angles of 64.3°–67.2°, indicating a stable gait rhythm. The running analysis revealed knee angles of 68.8°–69.8° and elbow angles of 87.6°–89.1°, indicating efficient propulsive mechanics. The flight phase demonstrated knee angles of 81.2°–87.8° and elbow angles of 80.4°–88.3°, suggesting effective momentum use and postural stability. These measurements supported stride-efficiency assessment and technique evaluation. Qualitative findings revealed that Kinovea enabled athletes to interpret movement phases and identify technical inefficiencies through slow-motion and frame-by-frame visualization. Conclusion: Kinovea supports basic motion analysis by providing clear kinematic information and helping beginner athletes observe and refine their movement techniques. The findings also offer practical value for coaches by enabling more precise identification of inefficient patterns and guiding targeted corrections during early-stage training.

title: A Review of Phishing Detection Techniques Using Machine Learning and Natural Language Processing
authors: Dr. Sunita Dixit
journal: Journal of Global Research in Multidisciplinary Studies(JGRMS)
abstract: The goal of phishing attacks, which rank high among cyber risks, is to steal sensitive information (such as login passwords, financial data, and more) from unsuspecting people and companies. Blacklist, whitelist, rule, heuristic, and signature-based detection methods are no longer suitable due to the rising sophistication of phishing schemes. As a result, ML, DL, and NLP are rapidly becoming into effective instruments for detecting both well-known and brand-new forms of phishing. Background on phishing assaults, old ways of detecting them, and recent advances in intelligent phishing detection are all included in this article. It delves into several machine learning algorithms such as decision tree, LSTM, ANN, CNN, and RNN, as well as deep learning models like KNN, NB, and SVM. Also, natural language processing methods including word embedding, sentiment analysis, text categorization, and tokenization are explored with the aim of detecting phishing material. Presenting a comprehensive, precise, and up-to-the-minute phishing detection system is the ultimate goal of this study, which focuses on machine learning frameworks, performance indicators, present obstacles, and future research directions.

abstract: In the context of increasing complexity of modern network infrastructures and the growing number of cyberattacks, improving the effectiveness of intrusion detection systems is a highly relevant task. The aim of this work is to develop and investigate a hybrid approach to network attack detection based on a combination of signature-based analysis and intelligent machine learning methods.  The research methods include analysis of requirements for anomaly detection systems, comparative analysis of existing solutions, design of a hybrid system architecture, and experimental modeling using multiclass classification of network traffic. The results demonstrate that integrating a neural model with a traditional detection system improves attack detection coverage and reduces the number of false positives.  The practical significance of the study lies in the possibility of deploying the proposed architecture in real corporate networks, while the theoretical significance consists in substantiating the effectiveness of a hybrid approach to traffic analysis. Future research directions include adaptive model training and expansion of the range of detectable attacks.

title: Transcatheter edge-to-edge repair in dynamic severe functional mitral regurgitation: A multicentre, randomised, controlled trial
authors: Bingzhen Li; Xiaojie Cai; Chao Li; Menghui Liu; Peihan Xie; Qian Zhou; Zhenyu Xiong; Cuiling Li; Fengjuan Yao; Min Ye; Wenjing Zhang; Junqi Zhong; Shaozhao Zhang; Xinxue Liao; Xiaodong Zhuang
journal: European Heart Journal - Valvular and Structural Heart Disease
abstract: Abstract Background Functional mitral regurgitation (FMR) is a highly dynamic disease. Some patients exhibit only moderate (2+) FMR at rest, which deteriorates to moderate-to-severe or severe FMR (3+ or 4+) during stress, with effective regurgitant orifice area (EROA) increased ≥0.1 cm2—termed dynamic severe FMR. Observational studies link this condition to worse outcomes, with mitral valve intervention offering potential benefits; however, high-quality evidence remains deficient. Aims The Transcatheter edge-to-edge repair In dynaMic sEvere functional mitral Regurgitation (TIMER) trial aims to assess the safety and effectiveness of transcatheter edge-to-edge repair plus guideline-directed medical therapy versus guideline-directed medical therapy alone in symptomatic chronic heart failure patients with dynamic severe FMR, defined as moderate (2+) regurgitation at rest (EROA ≥0.2 cm2 to <0.3 cm2 and/or regurgitant volume (RVol) ≥30 mL/beat to <45 mL/beat), deteriorating to moderate-to-severe or severe (3+ or 4+) during handgrip stress echocardiography (stress EROA ≥0.30 cm2 and/or RVol ≥45 mL/beat), with EROA increased ≥0.1 cm2. Methods This prospective, multicentre, randomised trial enrols patients with dynamic severe FMR confirmed by a core laboratory using handgrip stress echocardiography, across 20 participating centres in China. Patients are randomised 1:1 to transcatheter edge-to-edge repair plus medical therapy or medical therapy alone. The primary endpoint is the composite incidence of cardiovascular death and all heart failure hospitalisations during the entire follow-up period. Conclusion This trial will provide critical evidence on transcatheter edge-to-edge repair in patients with dynamic severe FMR, informing future treatment recommendations. Trial registration number: NCT07197021

title: CT and MRI in periprocedural transcatheter mitral valve replacement: expert recommendations by the European Society of Cardiovascular Radiology (ESCR) and the North American Society for Cardiovascular Imaging (NASCI)
authors: Anna Palmisano; Marco Francone; Prabhakar Shantha Rajiah; Jonathon Leipsic; Gudrun Maria Feuchtner; Matthias Eberhard; Ricardo P.J. Budde; Bradley D. Allen; Hatem Alkadhi; Antonio Esposito
abstract: Abstract Transcatheter mitral valve replacement (TMVR) is a minimally invasive treatment option for symptomatic patients with severe mitral valve disease who are at high surgical risk or ineligible for open-heart surgery. The procedure has been associated with improved quality of life and functional status in selected patients and is increasingly recognized as a valuable therapeutic option in the management of complex mitral valve disorders. A multidisciplinary Heart Team is essential to ensure the clinical success of TMVR, and imaging specialists play a central role in the preprocedural assessment for patient and device selection, during the procedure, to guide and monitor the implantation, and after the procedure, for follow-up and for the correct diagnosis of short- or long-term complications. Echocardiography is required for initial diagnosis, for assessment of valve hemodynamics, intraprocedural guidance and monitoring. However, a multimodality approach including CT and/or MRI is frequently needed to correctly manage the phase of preprocedural planning and the diagnosis of complications. This consensus document, developed by a working group of experts from the European Society of Cardiovascular Radiology (ESCR) and the North American Society for Cardiovascular Imaging (NASCI), provides evidence-based recommendations for CT and cardiac MRI acquisition and post-processing in procedural planning and postprocedural evaluation in patients undergoing TMVR. Emphasis is placed on the technical requirements and standardization of imaging protocols, which must account for the heterogeneity of imaging equipment used in clinical settings. The document also outlines recommendations for all necessary preprocedural measures to ensure consistency, accuracy, and effective communication among specialists. Key Points Question How can CT and MRI acquisition, measurement, and reporting for TMVR be standardized to support accurate procedural planning, device selection, and follow-up ? Findings This expert consensus provides recommendations for standardized CT and MRI protocols, key measurements, and structured reporting throughout TMVR planning and follow-up . Clinical relevance CT and MRI assessment may improve patient selection, procedural planning, multidisciplinary communication, and detection of postprocedural complications, supporting safer and more consistent TMVR practice across centers .

title: Mechanosensing channels PIEZO1 and PIEZO2 regulate mitral valve serotonin-mediated homeostasis and pathophysiology
authors: Stanley Stachelek; Robert LEVY; Emily Hall
abstract: Mitral regurgitation (MR) pathophysiology involves increased serotonin (5-HT) receptor (HTR) expression and signalling, together with reduced 5-HT transporter (SLC6A4) expression in mitral valve interstitial cells (MVIC). The mechanosensitive calcium channels, PIEZO1 and PIEZO2, regulate cellular responses to a variety of mechanical conditions; however, PIEZO1 and PIEZO2 have not been studied in MR. We investigated the hypothesis that PIEZO1 and PIEZO2 mediate, through 5-HT mechanisms, both homeostasis in normal mitral valves (nMV) and in the pathophysiology of MR.

title: Making Reynolds-number reasoning visible: complementary classroom models for plume organization and geometry–flow coupling
authors: Victor Akinyemi; Heidi L. Lujan; Stephen E. DiCarlo
abstract: Reynolds number is central to cardiovascular physiology, yet students often memorize the equation without understanding the competing inertial and viscous effects that it represents. We developed two complementary, low-cost classroom demonstrations intended to make selected relationships relevant to Reynolds-number reasoning visible without treating either apparatus as a quantitative Reynolds experiment. In the first, an adjustable aquarium air pump drives bubbles through submerged diffusers in transparent chambers. Changes in nominal pump drive and fluid composition produce qualitative changes in bubble rise, plume width, lateral motion, and plume organization. Because this is buoyant two-phase flow, these observations are not classifications of laminar or turbulent internal flow. In the second, aerosol generated by ultrasonic foggers is carried through nominal 5-mL and 50-mL serological pipettes and illuminated at the outlets. Changing pipette geometry changes flow resistance and can alter volumetric flow, internal and exit velocity, and jet momentum flux, but these quantities were not measured. The visible output is the external free jet; therefore, plume speed and coherence are described as apparent, qualitative observations rather than direct measures of internal velocity or Reynolds number. The activities use a predict-observe-explain sequence and connect cautiously to clinical examples as mechanistic analogies. This report describes qualitative instructional demonstrations, not a quantitative fluid-mechanics study or a formal educational-outcomes study.

title: Left coronary ostial embolization by a migrated pledget after redo mitral valve replacement: a case report
authors: Tongkai Ge; Danjie Luo; Jimei Chen; Xiaofeng Li
abstract: Redo mitral valve replacement is associated with increased surgical complexity and perioperative risk. Acute coronary obstruction caused by retained surgical materials is extremely rare but can lead to fatal myocardial ischemia. A 64-year-old woman with prior bioprosthetic mitral valve replacement underwent redo surgery for severe intraprosthetic regurgitation. Shortly after separation from cardiopulmonary bypass, she developed ventricular fibrillation and severe myocardial dysfunction, requiring reinstitution of bypass and subsequent extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO). Coronary angiography revealed a thrombus-like lesion at the left coronary ostium with preserved TIMI grade 3 flow; however, repeated aspiration failed to retrieve thrombotic material. Intravascular ultrasound demonstrated a solid non-thrombotic intraluminal obstruction. Surgical exploration confirmed complete occlusion of the left coronary ostium by a retained pledget from the previous operation. Removal of the pledget resulted in rapid improvement of myocardial contractility, and ECMO was successfully discontinued the following day. Coronary ostial embolization by retained pledget is a rare but life-threatening complication after redo mitral valve surgery. Early recognition, intravascular imaging, and timely surgical intervention with mechanical circulatory support are crucial for favorable outcomes.

title: Echocardiographic findings in children with Sydenham chorea: a retrospective cross-sectional study
authors: Tesfaye Taye Gelaw; Habtamu Bayih Engida
abstract: In children with Sydenham chorea (SC), the prevalence of carditis (both clinical and subclinical carditis) is significant. Though SC often appears as an isolated manifestation, echocardiography frequently reveals valvular damage that goes undetected on auscultation. Determine the prevalence and patterns of clinical and subclinical carditis in children with Sydenham’s chorea at Tibebe-Ghion and Adinas General Hospitals. A retrospective, cross-sectional analysis of the archived echocardiographic findings of all children (aged 5–15) diagnosed with Sydenham chorea from June 2019 to March 2026 was done between July 8, 2026, and August 7, 2026. A multinomial logistic regression done using SPSS version 27 evaluated the associations between age, sex, and carditis status. Associations were reported as odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals and significance at p < 0.05. Among 109 children with Sydenham chorea (mean age 10.07 ± 2.72 years; 59% female), 18% had no carditis, 66% had subclinical carditis, and 16% had clinical carditis. Mitral regurgitation (MR) was present in 82% of patients, primarily within the subclinical category (81%), with mild MR dominating subclinical cases (94%). Aortic regurgitation (AR) occurred in 22% of children, and 22% experienced combined MR and AR; isolated AR was not observed. Multinomial logistic regression demonstrated that neither age ( p = 0.929) nor sex ( p = 0.440) were significant predictors of carditis status. Echocardiography identified subclinical carditis in a substantial proportion of children with Sydenham chorea. These findings support the use of echocardiographic assessment in children with Sydenham chorea, particularly in high-burden settings. Not applicable.

title: Body Weight- and Age-Adjusted Reference Model for Septal Mitral Annular Plane Systolic Excursion in Healthy Dogs
abstract: Mitral annular plane systolic excursion (MAPSE) is an M-mode index of left ventricular longitudinal systolic motion.In dogs, interpretation of raw MAPSE is affected by wide body size variation; and the independent effect of age after body weight adjustment has not been quantified.This study aimed to develop a body weight-and age-adjusted reference model for septal MAPSE and derive normalized indices.This two-center retrospective study included 180 client-owned healthy dogs examined between November 2016 and December 2023.Inclusion criteria included the absence of structural cardiac abnormalities, sinus rhythm, systolic blood pressure <140mmHg, and no clinically relevant thoracic radiographic, hematologic, or biochemical abnormalities.Septal MAPSE was measured by M-mode echocardiography from the apical four-chamber view and averaged over three cycles.Multiple linear regression modeled log₁₀(MAPSE), using log₁₀(body weight) and age.Heart rate and sex/neuter status were assessed as additional covariates, and study center was assessed for systematic center-related differences.Model-based Z-scores and percentage of predicted MAPSE values were calculated.The final model was log₁₀(MAPSE)=0.6279+0.3243×log₁₀(BW)-0.008767×age,explaining 70.2% of variation in log₁₀(MAPSE).Body weight and age were significant predictors (P<0.0001).Predicted MAPSE scaled allometrically with body weight and decreased by 2.0% per year.Z-scores and percentage of predicted MAPSE showed no residual association with body weight or age.Septal MAPSE in healthy dogs is body weightand age-dependent.This model provides body weight-and age-adjusted expected values for interpreting septal MAPSE within the range represented by this cohort.

title: Estimated cumulative LDL-C exposure and severity of coronary artery lesions in patients with acute coronary syndrome: a retrospective observational cross-sectional analysis
authors: Caijie Dong; Lixiang Ma; Fu’e Zhang; Qi Qi; Wenli Kang; Zhian Jiang
abstract: Background Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease dominated by coronary atherosclerosis is the leading cause of global mortality and disability. Low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) is a well-established pathogenic driver, yet most existing studies rely on single cross-sectional LDL-C testing. Estimated cumulative LDL-C exposure, calculated as a single fasting LDL-C measurement multiplied by age and serving as a proxy for lifelong lipid burden, remains insufficiently characterized regarding its association with coronary lesion severity. Methods This retrospective observational cross-sectional analysis enrolled 871 patients with acute coronary syndrome (ACS) undergoing coronary angiography between January and September 2024. Estimated cumulative LDL-C exposure was calculated as fasting LDL-C measured within 24 h of admission (mmol/L) multiplied by age (years) and stratified into quartiles. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression was used for variable screening. Multiple linear regression, restricted cubic spline (RCS), subgroup interaction, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analyses were performed to quantify associations and predictive performance. Results Estimated cumulative LDL-C exposure was positively associated with the square root of the SYNTAX score ( β = 0.0098, P < 0.001). In covariate-adjusted ROC analyses, the model containing estimated cumulative LDL-C exposure showed slightly higher discrimination than the model containing age and LDL-C as separate additive terms (AUC 0.860 vs. 0.853; DeLong P = 0.0160), although the absolute difference was small (ΔAUC = 0.007). RCS analysis identified a nonlinear association ( P for nonlinearity = 0.026) with a point of maximum estimated slope at approximately 170.2 mmol·year/L; however, the 95% confidence interval was wide (56.6–177.9 mmol·year/L), and this value should not be interpreted as a validated threshold. Subgroup interaction tests revealed stronger associations in male patients and smokers (sex P = 0.036; smoking P = 0.047 both after FDR correction). Conclusions Estimated cumulative LDL-C exposure was independently associated with greater coronary lesion severity in patients with acute coronary syndrome. The estimated cumulative LDL-C exposure model showed modestly better fit and discrimination than the age + LDL-C model, although this finding should be interpreted cautiously because age is mathematically embedded in the exposure definition. These findings are consistent with the cumulative LDL-C exposure hypothesis and support its potential value in assessing coronary lesion burden.

title: Advanced Hemodynamic Monitoring During Cesarean Section for Placenta Accreta Spectrum in a Pregnant Patient With Cardiac Disease and an Elevated BMI
authors: Georgia Ntalamagka; Giolanda Varvarousi; Emmanouil Stamatakis; Michail Pavlidis; Dimitrios Valsamidis
abstract: Placenta accreta spectrum (PAS) in parturients with significant cardiovascular disease presents major anesthetic and hemodynamic challenges, particularly when complicated by obesity and a high risk of hemorrhage.We report the successful perioperative management of a 42-year-old parturient at 35 weeks of gestation with repaired patent foramen ovale, hypertensive cardiomyopathy with reduced left ventricular ejection fraction (40%), regional left ventricular wall motion abnormalities, moderate mitral regurgitation, obesity, and lumbar degenerative disc disease who underwent cesarean delivery under advanced hemodynamic monitoring.Regional anesthesia was selected over general anesthesia to minimize myocardial depression, sympathetic stimulation, and postoperative respiratory complications.A low-dose combined spinal-epidural technique was administered with gradual epidural extension to a T4 sensory level.Continuous invasive hemodynamic monitoring using the Hypotension Prediction Index (HPI; HemoSphere, 7.6 advanced monitoring platform from BD; software version 3.1) provided continuous assessment of cardiac output, stroke volume, systemic vascular resistance, dynamic arterial elastance, and left ventricular contractility (dP/dt).Norepinephrine was initiated immediately following intrathecal anesthesia and titrated to maintain arterial pressure and systemic vascular resistance close to baseline values, thereby minimizing the risk of neuraxial anesthesiainduced hypotension and potential myocardial hypoperfusion.The surgical procedure was complicated by dense pelvic adhesions, difficult bladder mobilization, and a prolonged skin-to-delivery interval of 12 minutes.Despite these challenges, hemodynamic stability was maintained throughout the procedure.Cardiac output increased from 5.5 L/min at baseline to 6.9 L/min following completion of epidural dosing, while stroke volume remained close to baseline.Although this change occurred temporally after completion of epidural dosing, a direct causal relationship could not be established from the available data.Following delivery, cardiac output decreased to 5.8 L/min without significant hemodynamic instability.Estimated blood loss was 1000 mL, and one unit of packed red blood cells was administered.Rotational thromboelastometry (ROTEM) analysis demonstrated preserved clot firmness and adequate fibrinogen contribution, with no evidence of clinically significant coagulopathy based on the available assessment.The neonate was delivered with an Apgar score of 8.This case highlights the potential value of combining carefully titrated neuraxial anesthesia with advanced hemodynamic monitoring in high-risk obstetric patients with cardiomyopathy and PAS.HPI-guided monitoring facilitated proactive vasopressor therapy and individualized hemodynamic management in a patient with limited cardiovascular reserve.Together, continuous hemodynamic assessment and point-ofcare ROTEM provided complementary information for cardiovascular and coagulation management.Further studies are needed to determine the role of HPI-guided management in parturients at high risk for hemorrhage and cardiovascular instability.

title: Maternally inherited PRKAR1A pathogenic variant causing Carney complex with a concomitant LDLR variant resulting in hyperlipidemia: a case report
authors: Caihong Guo; Hongwei Yi; Yujing Yang; Caiping Han; Qingkun Fan; Jie Wang; Chenggang Deng
abstract: Objective Carney complex (CNC) is an autosomal dominant multisystem tumor syndrome predominantly caused by pathogenic PRKAR1A mutations. Cardiac myxoma, multiple endocrine neoplasms and cutaneous pigmented lesions are its typical clinical manifestations. We report an extremely uncommon case of CNC caused by a PRKAR1A pathogenic variant, with a LDLR variant leading to familial hyperlipidemia and marked phenotypic heterogeneity within the family. Case presentation A 45-year-old male presented with palpitations was admitted to our hospital. The patient’s past medical history included cerebral infarction, myocardial infarction, right monocular blindness, and atrial myxoma. Physical examination revealed typical acromegalic facies, accompanied by markedly elevated serum growth hormone (GH) levels. Pituitary magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) further identified a pituitary neuroendocrine tumor. Transthoracic echocardiography and contrast-enhanced cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) with late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) demonstrated global cardiac chamber enlargement and ventricular hypertrophy. Coronary CTA revealed diffuse dilatation of the coronary artery. Genetic testing confirmed two maternally inherited pathogenic variants: the splice-donor variant PRKAR1A c.769 + 1G>A responsible for CNC, and LDLR c.1879G>A, which causes familial hypercholesterolemia. One month after discharge from our hospital, the patient received transnasal transsphenoidal resection of sellar pituitary lesion under general anesthesia at the Department of Neurosurgery in another general hospital. Preoperative GH and insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1) were elevated on repeat testing, and both decreased significantly postoperatively. The sellar lesion was confirmed as a plurihormonal pituitary neuroendocrine tumor of pituitary transcription factor 1 (PIT-1) lineage; immunohistochemistry showed weak GH expression, focal prolactin (PRL) and luteinizing hormone (LH) expression, negative adrenocorticotropic hormone(ACTH) and T-box pituitary transcription factor(T-PIT) staining, with a Ki-67 labeling index of ~1%. Conclusion The splice-site variant PRKAR1A c.769 + 1G>A represents a well-documented recurrent pathogenic variant among patients with CNC. The majority of previously reported carriers develop primary pigmented nodular adrenocortical disease (PPNAD) and overt Cushing syndrome. However, our patient presented with acromegaly driven by a plurihormonal PIT-1-lineage pituitary neuroendocrine tumor without corticotroph differentiation. accompanied by atrial myxoma, cardiac hypertrophy, cardiomegaly, coronary dilatation, and familial hypercholesterolemia secondary to an LDLR mutation. This rare coexisting genetic phenotype underscores the value of prompt genetic and endocrine screening for at-risk patients.

title: Surgical Managment of a Forearm Arteriovenous Fistula in a Child with Noonan Syndrome: A Case Report
authors: Galib Bairamovi; Adem İlkay Diken
abstract: Peripheral arteriovenous fistulas (AVFs) are rare vascular anomalies in children and typically result from trauma or iatrogenic injury.To the best of our knowledge, we report the first case of a peripheral AVF associated with genetically confirmed CBL syndrome (Noonan syndrome-like disorder).A 5-year-old boy with CBL syndrome presented with a two-week history of progressive swelling, prominent superficial veins, and a palpable thrill in the right forearm.He had no known history of trauma or invasive procedures involving the affected extremity.Genetic testing had revealed a heterozygous pathogenic variant in the CBL gene (c.1100A>C,p.Gln367Pro).Physical examination revealed marked swelling in the antecubital region, dilated tortuous veins, a strong continuous thrill over the antecubital fossa, and an audible vascular bruit.Distal pulses were intact with no signs of ischemia.Computed tomography angiography demonstrated a direct abnormal connection between the brachial artery and basilic vein at the antecubital level.Color Doppler ultrasonography confirmed arterialized venous flow patterns.Comprehensive preoperative coagulation studies were within the normal limits.Under general anesthesia, surgical exploration identified a 5 mm wide fistulous connection between the brachial artery and basilic vein.The fistula was primarily repaired with 7-0 polypropylene sutures.Postoperatively, the thrill disappeared with preserved distal pulses.Postoperative Doppler ultrasonography confirmed complete fistula closure.At one-year followup, the patient remained asymptomatic with excellent extremity perfusion and no evidence of recurrence.Cranial magnetic resonance imaging and thoracic computed tomography revealed no evidence of intracranial or intrathoracic vascular malformations on available imaging.This case expands the vascular phenotype of RASopathies and suggests a link between RAS-MAPK dysregulation and peripheral AVF development.Clinicians should maintain heightened awareness for peripheral vascular anomalies in syndromic patients, even without a trauma history.

title: One-Year Outcomes of Patients Diagnosed with Peripartum dialted Cardiomyopathy: A 5-Year Multicenter Retrospective Cohort Study in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia
authors: Thomas Atanfu; Kindalem Fentie; Fraol Daba Chinkey; Weys Neda; ABIGIYA BERASSA; Desalew Mekonnen
abstract: Abstract Background: Peripartum cardiomyopathy (PPCM) is an important cause of maternal heart failure associated with variable recovery and significant morbidity and mortality. Outcomes significantly differ from region to region with lower in high-income settings and very high in Africa and Asia. However, data from Ethiopia remain limited, particularly regarding one-year clinical and echocardiographic outcomes. Objective: To assess the one-year clinical and echocardiographic outcomes of patients diagnosed with peripartum cardiomyopathy and to identify factors associated with poor outcomes. Methods: A multicenter retrospective cohort study was conducted across selected tertiary and private hospitals in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. All women diagnosed with PPCM between January 2020 and December 2024 were included using a census sampling approach. Data were extracted from electronic medical records and supplemented by phone follow-up when necessary. The primary outcomes were one-year mortality, heart failure–related hospital admission, and one-year ejection fraction recovery. A composite poor outcome was defined as death, hospital admission, or non-recovery of left ventricular function. Results: A total of 61 patients were included in the analysis. Five patients (8.2%) died within one year of diagnosis. Among patients with available one-year echocardiographic data, 50.8% achieved recovery of left ventricular systolic function. The remaining patients demonstrated either partial recovery or persistent systolic dysfunction. Higher baseline New York Heart Association (NYHA) functional class (III–IV) was associated with poorer outcomes, including lower rates of ejection fraction recovery and increased likelihood of adverse clinical outcomes. Conclusion: PPCM in this Ethiopia’s associated with measurable mortality, significant morbidity and heterogeneous recovery of left ventricular function at one year. Only about half of patients achieved full recovery, with worse outcomes observed among those presenting with advanced heart failure and severely reduced ejection fraction. Outcomes appear more favorable than those reported in some African settings but remain inferior to those observed in high-income countries.

title: Mitral valve disease in rheumatic heart disease, systemic lupus erythematosus, antiphospholipid syndrome, and rheumatoid Arthritis
authors: Mateusz Lucki; Bogna Grygiel‐Górniak; Ewa Lucka; Maciej Lesiak
abstract: Mitral valve disease occurs in rheumatic heart disease (RHD) and selected systemic autoimmune rheumatic diseases, but similar lesions may have different underlying mechanisms. This structured narrative review examines epidemiological, mechanistic, imaging, and management evidence, distinguishing established pathways from incompletely validated mechanisms and hypotheses. In RHD, post-streptococcal valvulitis leads to fibrotic remodeling, commissural fusion, and chordal shortening, producing mitral stenosis, regurgitation, or mixed disease. A meta-analysis of 215,552 children and adolescents in endemic settings reported echocardiographically detected RHD in 24 per 1000. In systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and antiphospholipid syndrome (APS), typical findings include leaflet thickening, Libman-Sacks vegetations, and regurgitation; embolic complications may occur despite mild valve dysfunction. Among 508 clinically selected patients with SLE undergoing echocardiography, 27.4% had heart valve involvement and 11.2% had mitral involvement. Immunothrombotic mechanisms may contribute to these lesions, but direct validation in human valve tissue remains incomplete. In rheumatoid arthritis (RA), a prospective cohort found an association with incident mitral regurgitation (adjusted hazard ratio 1.54, 95% confidence interval 1.32-1.81), but not mitral stenosis. Myocardial imaging findings do not establish a causal link to regurgitation. These findings support anatomy- and severity-based assessment in RHD, combined valvular and thromboembolic evaluation in SLE/APS, and assessment of conventional regurgitation mechanisms in RA. The framework informs clinical interpretation within existing guidelines, while proposed disease-specific mechanisms require further validation.

title: A Study on the Correlation Between Malnutrition and Short-Term Prognosis in Elderly Emergency Admissions
authors: Meng Yang; Zhang Shu
abstract: Abstract Background Malnutrition affects patients health and clinical prognosis in multiple ways. Approximately one-quarter of older adults worldwide are at risk of malnutrition or suffer from malnutrition. Malnutrition and malnutrition risk are highly prevalent in emergency patients and are associated with adverse clinical outcomes. However, nutritional risk assessment is not routinely performed for elderly emergency patients in clinical practice, and studies on the nutritional status of elderly emergency patients remain scarce. The short-term prognostic significance of malnutrition in elderly Chinese emergency admissions remains unclear. Methods This retrospective study collected clinical data of elderly patients (≥ 60 years) who visited the Emergency Department of West China Hospital, Sichuan University between May 31, 2019 and December 31, 2023 and were admitted to hospital within 72 hours. We first characterized the nutritional status of elderly patients admitted via the emergency department. Patients were then divided into a malnutrition group and a normal nutrition group based on GNRI and GLIM. PSM was used to match the two groups at the 1:1 ratio. The 28-day survival was compared between the two groups, and short-term survival curves were plotted using the Kaplan–Meier method. Secondary outcomes, including ICU admission rate and total length of hospital stay, were also compared to analyze the impact of malnutrition on short-term prognosis in elderly emergency admissions. Results A total of 7,439 patients were included after applying inclusion and exclusion criteria. According to GNRI assessment, 43.3% of patients had nutritional risk. The nutritional risk group showed statistically significant differences in ICU admission, length of hospital stay, and 28-day mortality compared with the no-risk group (P < 0.05). A total of 4,217 patients without nutritional risk by GNRI were assigned to the normal nutrition group, and 1,658 patients diagnosed with malnutrition by GLIM were assigned to the malnutrition group. Malnutrition significantly reduced 28-day survival in elderly patients (P < 0.001). After PSM, 1,375 patients were successfully matched in each group, with acceptable between-group balance. After adjusting for covariates, the malnutrition group had significantly lower 28-day survival than the normal nutrition group (P = 0.068). There was no significant difference in ICU admission rate between the normal nutrition and malnutrition groups (P = 0.303), while malnutrition significantly prolonged the length of hospital stay (P < 0.001). Conclusions Nutritional risk/malnutrition is common in elderly emergency admissions. Elderly emergency admissions with malnutrition have longer hospital stays and lower 28-day survival rates than those with normal nutrition, with no significant difference in ICU admission rate.

title: Frailty management in patients with heart valve disease: a scoping review
authors: Wenhui Yuan; HAN Qiong; Peihuang Dong; Xinglin Zheng; Yuan Chen; Linjing Wu
abstract: Purpose This study aims to identify, evaluate, and summarise evidence on frailty management in patients with valvular heart disease to inform the development of frailty management programs for clinical practice. Methods This study adheres to the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) framework and is reported in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR) guidelines to guarantee methodological strictness and transparency. The system searched multiple databases and websites to gather evidence on the management of frailty in patients with heart valve disease. The search covered the period from the database's inception to October 2026. Literature screening, quality assessment, evidence extraction, and synthesis were conducted independently by two researchers, and the evidence was graded using the JBI Evidence Grading System (2014 edition). Results After a rigorous literature screening process, a total of 28 publications were included, comprising 3 clinical guidelines, 12 expert consensus documents, 1 systematic review, 1 evidence summary, 6 observational studies, 4 randomised controlled trials, and 1 quasi-experimental study. Through a systematic synthesis of the included literature, a total of 46 pieces of evidence were ultimately compiled, covering five areas: identification and screening assessment of the risk of frailty, comprehensive management, exercise rehabilitation management, multidimensional support management, and continuity of rehabilitation care. Conclusion The 46 pieces of evidence summarised in this study can serve as an evidence-based reference for clinical healthcare professionals when developing frailty management programs; however, as this evidence has not yet been systematically implemented in clinical practice, its effectiveness continues to be further validated by future research. Systematic Review Registration http://ebn.nursing.fudan.edu.cn/home , identifier ES20259514.

title: Transcatheter Closure of Paravalvular Leak Using a Dedicated Occluder Device: Our Initial Experience with Occlutech PLD Occluder in a Complex Redo-Aortic Patient
authors: K.C. Ng; L.S. Chen; K.T. Lee; A.W. Mohamed Jahangir; J. Mohammad Tamim
abstract: BACKGROUND Paravalvular leak (PVL) following surgical aortic valve replacement is associated with significant morbidity, including heart failure and transfusion-dependent haemolytic anaemia. Transcatheter device closure, in contrast to surgical treatment, is a well-recognized treatment option due to its safer complication and mortality profiles. However, regional data and local experience showed that most PVL closures were done using non-dedicated devices which are not purposefully engineered to meet its specific pathology and anatomical complexity. OBJECTIVE To evaluate the feasibility and demonstrate procedural outcome using the Occlutech PLD Occluder device, a dedicated PVL closure device. CASE SUMMARY A 52-year-old man with prior Stanford type A aortic dissection repair, and redo aortic arch replacement with bioprosthetic aortic valve replacement, presented with progressive dyspnoea and transfusion-dependent haemolytic anaemia. Echocardiography confirmed the presence of PVL which was successfully closed with transcatheter strategy, using an Occlutech PLD 61PLD8W Occluder. RESULTS The Occlutech PLD Occluder device was successfully deployed with satisfactory results leading to significant improvement in patient’s symptoms. CONCLUSION The usage of a dedicated PVL closure device yielded positive outcome in our early experience, and supports broader availability and further evaluation of dedicated PVL closure devices in this setting.

title: Female Fingerprint: Sex-Specific Aspects in Patients With Atrial Fibrillation and Heart Failure
authors: Esther Roth; Laura Rottner
abstract: Abstract Purpose of Review Atrial fibrillation (AF) and heart failure (HF) frequently coexist and represent a major source of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. This review summarizes current evidence on sex-specific differences in epidemiology, pathophysiology, clinical presentation, prognosis, and treatment in women with AF and HF. Recent Findings Emerging evidence indicates that women with AF and HF constitute a distinct clinical and biological phenotype. Women typically develop AF at older age, more commonly present with hypertension and HF with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), and report greater symptom burden and impaired quality of life. Sex-specific mechanisms including hormonal influences, atrial fibrosis, endothelial dysfunction, inflammation, autonomic dysregulation, and microvascular disease contribute to these differences. Population studies further demonstrate sex-related disparities in HF development and outcomes across AF subtypes. Summary Despite increasing awareness, women remain underrepresented in clinical trials and are less likely to receive rhythm-control strategies, catheter ablation, or device therapy. Recognition of the “female fingerprint” in AF and HF is essential for individualized risk stratification and the advancement of precision cardiovascular medicine.

title: Serum creatinine- and cystatin C-derived sarcopenia-related indices and the risk of all-cause mortality in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation
authors: Yu Wang; Guipeng An; Xiangjuan Liu; Lianyue Ma; Xiao Meng; Huixia Lu; Mei Dong
abstract: Background Sarcopenia is increasingly recognized as an important predictor of adverse outcomes after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI). However, the prognostic relevance of sarcopenia-related indices derived from serum creatinine and cystatin C in patients undergoing TAVI has not been fully established. Methods This prospective study included 465 patients who underwent TAVI for symptomatic aortic stenosis. Associations between sarcopenia-related indices and all-cause mortality were assessed using Kaplan–Meier survival analysis, Cox proportional hazards models, and restricted cubic spline analysis (RCS). Predictive performance and incremental prognostic value were compared across indices using time-dependent receiver operating characteristic curves (ROC), the Harrell’s C-index, net reclassification improvement (NRI), and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI). Subgroup and sensitivity analyses were performed to examine the robustness of the findings. Results During a median follow-up of 2.8 years, 59 (12.7%) deaths occurred. In the fully adjusted Cox model, each 1-standard deviation increase in eGFRcys/eGFRcr (HR 0.29, 95% CI 0.11–0.75; p = 0.011) and Cr * eGFRcys (HR 0.30, 95% CI 0.14–0.64; p = 0.002) was associated with a lower risk of all-cause mortality. Time-dependent ROC indicated that Cr * eGFRcys had the most favorable predictive performance among the evaluated indices. Adding Cr * eGFRcys to the fully adjusted model increased the concordance index from 0.696 to 0.736 and significantly improved risk reclassification and discrimination (NRI: 0.437, 95% CI 0.171–0.704, p = 0.001; IDI: 0.026, 95% CI 0.004–0.048, p = 0.022). Findings from subgroup and sensitivity analyses were broadly consistent. Conclusion Among patients with symptomatic aortic stenosis undergoing TAVI, lower eGFRcys/eGFRcr and Cr * eGFRcys were associated with a higher risk of all-cause mortality after the procedure. Notably, Cr * eGFRcys showed stronger prognostic value and may provide additional prognostic information for risk stratification in patients undergoing TAVI.

title: miR-26b in vascular calcification: transcriptomic insights and its potential as an Aortic Stenosis biomarker
authors: Rosa Bauzà Sansó
abstract: Aortic stenosis (AS) is a progressive cardiovascular condition and one of the most frequent valvular diseases in ageing populations. It is characterised by the narrowing of the aortic valve opening, sometimes referred to as a failing heart valve. Despite its high prevalence, the molecular mechanisms underlying it are still not completely understood, and there are no reliable biomarkers for its early detection or risk stratification. One of the key features in AS pathophysiology is vascular calcification (VC), an active, cell-regulated process involving both endothelial and immune cells. Understanding this process at the molecular level may be crucial to unlocking new therapeutic and diagnostic avenues. MicroRNAs (miRNAs), small non-coding RNAs, have emerged as relevant regulators of gene expression in cardiovascular disease. MiR-26b has been associated with vascular calcification, and miR-26b knock-out mice (KO) developed spontaneous age-related aortic microcalcifications. However, the specific mechanisms of miR-26 b in AS remain unclear. This thesis investigates the role of miR-26b in endothelial and immune cell function within VC using both bioinformatics and experimental approaches and assesses its potential as a circulating biomarker for AS. Single-cell transcriptomics was performed using single-cell RNA sequencing datasets from miR-26b knock-out mice, focusing on endothelial and immune cell populations. Functional enrichment and crosstalk analyses were conducted to identify pathways related to miR-26 b. These findings were validated through in vitro transfection of miR-26b inhibitors in aortic endothelial cells, permeability assays, and flow cytometry of immune cell populations. As previous data showed an inverse correlation between microRNA-26b (miR26b) levels and the degree of calcification in aortic and valve tissue from patients with AS and aortic disease, the potential of miR-26b as a circulating biomarker for patients with AS and atherosclerosis was investigated. A well-characterised dataset of plasma samples was used to assess whether miR-26b can predict disease severity and how various atherosclerotic risk factors may influence the progression of AS. The dataset comprises clinical outcomes from 95 patients with various AS stages and age-matched controls (the SALTIRE 3 cohort at the University of Edinburgh – clinicaltrials.gov: NCT06047561). miR-26b expression was obtained from patients' plasma RNA using RT-qPCRs and analysed using computational tools for statistical analysis and correlation assessments. No correlation was found between the circulation miR-26b expression and CT Calcium Score. Lipoprotein A levels, a known cardiovascular factor, were suggested as a possible correlating factor with miR-26b, especially in females and patients with severe AS. Together, these results suggest that miR-26b plays a regulatory role in the behaviour of endothelial and immune cells during vascular calcification, highlighting its potential as a non-invasive biomarker for aortic stenosis.

title: Correlation analysis of left atrial appendage morphology and function with ischemic stroke in patients with non-valvular atrial fibrillation
authors: Shi Peiqing; Yanhan Wang; XU Ding-hu; Chen Jinan; Jiang Ya-bin; Jimeng Yang; Jun Wang
abstract: Abstract Objective: The aim of this study is to analyze the correlations between left atrial appendage (LAA) morphology, LAA function, and other clinical factors with ischemic stroke in patients with non-valvular atrial fibrillation (NVAF). Methods: This single-center prospective observational study enrolled consecutive NVAF patients who underwent contrast-enhanced left atrial CT at the Department of Cardiology, Jiangning Hospital Affiliated to Nanjing Medical University from July 2021 to August 2022. Clinical and imaging data were collected at baseline. Survivors were followed annually for a minimum of two years, including repeat cranial CT. Patients were divided into two groups: those without new ischemic stroke during follow-up (Group A) and those with new ischemic stroke (Group B). Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis was utilized to assess the predictive performance of the CHA2DS2-VASc score alone and in combination with LAA depth and LAA slow blood flow for new ischemic stroke; results are reported as area under the ROC curve (AUC). Results: A total of 100 patients completed the study, with 85 in Group A and 15 in Group B. Group B had significantly higher CHA2DS2-VASc scores, prevalence of hypertension history, statin use, LAA depth, left superior pulmonary vein long diameter, left superior pulmonary vein short diameter, incidence of left atrial thrombus, and LAA slow blood flow (all P < 0.05). Multivariable logistic regression identified hypertension history (OR = 1.092; 95% CI, 1.003–1.188; P = 0.042), LAA depth (OR = 27.923; 95% CI, 1.807–431.513; P = 0.017), and LAA slow blood flow (OR = 5.917; 95% CI, 1.349–25.952; P = 0.018) as independent risk factors for ischemic stroke during follow-up. The AUCs for predicting new ischemic stroke were 0.713 for the CHA2DS2-VASc score alone and 0.825 for the CHA2DS2-VASc score combined with LAA depth and LAA slow blood flow. Conclusion: In patients with NVAF, the risk of ischemic stroke is significant. Furthermore, integrating LAA depth and LAA slow-flow parameters with the CHA2DS2-VASc score substantially enhances its predictive ability for stroke compared to the CHA2DS2-VASc score alone.

title: Device-detected new-onset atrial fibrillation after dual-chamber pacemaker implantation in patients with sick sinus syndrome under managed ventricular pacing: a risk nomogram from the 3-month landmark
authors: Jin-Mei Xie; Cheng-Hua Shan; Ying-Jun Xiao; Jie Ma; Ren-Rong Lü; Zong-Jie Zheng
abstract: Background New-onset atrial fibrillation ( N OAF) is common after dual-chamber pacemaker implantation, but existing prediction models were derived from mixed populations of patients with sick sinus syndrome (SSS) and atrioventricular block and included heterogeneous pacing strategies. Methods In this single-centre retrospective cohort study, consecutive patients with SSS who received a first permanent Medtronic dual-chamber pacemaker with managed ventricular pacing (MVP) enabled as the default strategy were screened. Patients with atrial fibrillation or an atrial high-rate episode (AHRE) within 3 months after implantation were excluded, and prediction time started at this 3-month landmark, with atrial pacing percentage (AP%) and ventricular pacing percentage (VP%) measured at that visit. Patients implanted in 2015–2021 formed the development cohort ( n = 322), and those implanted in 2022–2025 formed a temporal validation cohort ( n = 121) reserved exclusively for validation. Twenty-six candidate predictors were assessed by univariable and multivariable Cox regression with backward Akaike information criterion (AIC) selection. Internal validation repeated the complete model-building procedure within 2,000 bootstrap samples. Temporal performance was assessed using discrimination and calibration at 1, 2 and 3 years after the landmark. Results NOAF occurred in 90 of 322 development patients (28.0%) during a median follow-up of 41.6 months [interquartile range (IQR), 13.7–80.1], and in 28 of 121 temporal validation patients (23.1%) during a median follow-up of 30.5 months (IQR, 8.8–45.9). Age (hazard ratio [HR] per year, 1.043; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.019–1.067), maximum P-wave duration (Pmax; HR per 10 ms, 1.200; 95% CI, 1.085–1.326), left atrial volume index (LAVi; HR per 1 mL/m2, 1.051; 95% CI, 1.030–1.073), AP% > 50% (HR, 1.845; 95% CI, 1.198–2.840) and VP% > 40% (HR, 1.898; 95% CI, 1.045–3.446) were independently associated with NOAF. The apparent C-index was 0.735; repeating the complete model-building procedure within 2,000 bootstrap samples gave a mean optimism of 0.036 and an optimism-corrected C-index of 0.6992. In temporal validation the C-index was 0.769 (95% CI, 0.639–0.873) and cumulative/dynamic AUC values were 0.753, 0.881 and 0.916 at 1, 2 and 3 years after the landmark. Calibration-in-the-large was −0.17, 0.24 and 0.35 and calibration slopes were 0.90, 0.99 and 0.98 at 1, 2 and 3 years, respectively. The 1-year calibration estimate remained least precise, with only five NOAF events by 1 year in the validation cohort. Conclusion In patients with SSS who remained free of atrial arrhythmia through the 3-month post-implantation landmark, a five-variable landmark model showed moderate optimism-corrected discrimination in the development cohort and promising same-centre temporal validation performance, particularly at 2 and 3 years after the landmark. The limited number of validation events, particularly at 1 year, warrants cautious interpretation. Prospective multicentre external validation is required before clinical implementation.

title: Interpretable machine learning for postoperative atrial fibrillation after noncardiac surgery
authors: Shuyi Zhu; Yigao Gao; Lin Li; Pingping Wang; Chaowei Zhang; Yunpeng Li; YingWei Chen
abstract: Abstract Postoperative atrial fibrillation (POAF) is an important complication after non-cardiac surgery and is associated with adverse short- and long-term outcomes. Accurate perioperative risk stratification remains challenging because POAF risk reflects both baseline atrial substrate and dynamic perioperative physiologic stress. We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the INSPIRE perioperative database to develop interpretable prediction models for clinically documented postoperative atrial fibrillation (POAF) after non-cardiac surgery. POAF was defined as new-onset AF captured during the index hospitalization by electrocardiography or rhythm-monitoring documentation; because a uniform cohort-wide measure of monitoring intensity was not available, the endpoint was interpreted as clinically detected POAF. Candidate predictors were grouped by acquisition window into preoperative, intraoperative, and early postoperative (≤ 24 h) variables to support dynamic perioperative risk assessment rather than a purely preoperative screen. Feature selection was performed with Boruta, model explanation with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), and classifier comparison with LASSO logistic regression, AdaBoost, LightGBM, XGBoost, and CatBoost. Because POAF was uncommon, performance was evaluated with AUROC, sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV, and F1 score after stratified splitting and threshold evaluation; synthetic resampling was not used in the primary analysis. Among 99,887 patients, 1,058 (1.1%) developed clinically documented POAF. Compared with controls, POAF cases were older (median 70 vs. 55 years) and showed substantially greater burdens of hypotension and hypoxemia, including more frequent and prolonged MAP < 65 mmHg and SpO₂ <90%. Boruta retained average diastolic blood pressure, average heart rate, and left atrial enlargement as informative features. SHAP identified valvular disease, surgical duration, cardiopulmonary instability, and related early postoperative events as major contributors, consistent with a dynamic perioperative risk model. Discrimination was good across classifiers, with AUCs ranging from 0.80 to 0.85. AdaBoost and CatBoost achieved the best overall performance (both AUC 0.85), while CatBoost showed higher specificity and PPV. In a large non-cardiac surgical cohort, clinically documented POAF was associated with both baseline atrial substrate and perioperative cardiopulmonary stress. Interpretable ML models, particularly boosting-based methods, showed good discrimination and may support dynamic perioperative risk updating and targeted postoperative surveillance, although monitoring heterogeneity, class imbalance, calibration, and external validation remain important considerations.

title: In-Hospital Stroke in Patients with Cardiac Conditions: Do Cardiac Procedures Impact Stroke Outcomes?
authors: Ameen Alizada; Rana Abdalrahman; Chitapa Kaveeta; Mohamad Mehdi; Dana Harris; Jillian M. Stang; Robert Moore; Mohamed A AlShamrani; Beatrice Agnelli; Jessalyn K. Holodinsky; Bijoy K. Menon; Michael D. Hill; Mohammed Almekhlafi; Katrina Hannah D. Ignacio
journal: Canadian Journal of Neurological Sciences / Journal Canadien des Sciences Neurologiques
abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: It is unclear if stroke occurring after cardiac procedures is more severe than stroke associated with cardiac conditions without procedures. We compared in-hospital acute ischemic stroke patients admitted with a cardiac diagnosis who did versus did not undergo cardiac procedures. METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, we analyzed adults with in-hospital stroke admitted with a primary cardiac diagnosis in Alberta (2018-2022). Patients were categorized into no prior cardiac procedure, cardiac procedure, or cardiac surgery within 30 days of stroke diagnosis. Multivariable logistic regression was used to assess associations between exposure groups and outcomes. RESULTS: Among 499 patients (median age 70 years IQR [62-77], 36.7% women), 116 (23.2%) underwent a cardiac procedure, and 227 (45.5%) underwent cardiac surgery prior to stroke diagnosis. Median time from procedure to stroke diagnosis was 1.75 days (IQR 0.87-3.83). In-hospital mortality was 34.6%, 24.1% and 22.5% in patients with no prior procedure, cardiac procedures and cardiac surgery, respectively. After adjustment for age, sex, facility level and comorbidities, no significant differences were observed in mortality (cardiac procedure vs no procedure: aOR 0.73, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.40-1.33; cardiac surgery vs no procedure: aOR 0.78, 95% CI 0.42-1.45). Among procedural patients, strokes recognized ≥2 days post-procedure were associated with higher mortality (2-7 days: OR 2.31, [1.18-4.52]; 8-30 days: OR 3.23, [1.59-6.59]). CONCLUSIONS: Adjusted mortality did not differ by cardiac procedural status, although residual confounding is possible. Later stroke recognition after cardiac procedures was associated with higher mortality, identifying a high-risk monitoring window.

title: Time to Storm the Next CASTLE: Can Atrial Fibrillation Ablation Improve Outcomes in Patients With Heart Failure and Preserved Ejection Fraction?
authors: Alex El Darzi; Maximilian Moersdorf; Michel Abou Khalil; Christian M. Massad; Mohammad Montaser Atasi; Yara Menassa; Carlo El Khoury; Nassir F. Marrouche
abstract: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and atrial fibrillation frequently coexist and are linked by shared mechanisms including atrial myopathy, elevated filling pressures, fibrosis, and adverse hemodynamic interactions. The combination of both diseases worsens patient outcomes, and catheter ablation has emerged as a potentially important treatment strategy in this population. This review aims to summarize and highlight the current evidence on ablation in patients with atrial fibrillation and HFpEF. RECENT FINDINGS: When examining outcomes of mortality, hospitalization, hemodynamics, and recurrence, ablation appears to be superior to medical treatment with some mixed results. However, no large trials have been conducted on the topic, and no clear guidelines for ablation in HFpEF patients exist. Ablation is promising but not yet definitive for patients with atrial fibrillation and HFpEF. Ongoing trials, including CASTLE-HFpEF should clarify the gaps including patient selection, procedural strategy, and outcome benefit.

title: Cardiac comorbidity role in the diagnosis of diabetes mellitus using single lead electrocardiogram utilizing machine learning model
authors: Anna Dmitrievna Karbovskaya; Basheer Abdullah Marzoog; Snezhana Nikolaevna Demchuk; Anastasia Stroeva; Daniil Andreevich Zelenov; Peter Chomakhidze; Natalia Kuznetsova; Syrkin Abromavich; Valentin V Fadeev; Irina V. Poluboyarinova; Sevindzh M Ismailova; Philipp Kopylov
abstract: BACKGROUNDCardiovascular disease alters electrocardiographic morphology and may obscure diabetes-related electrical signatures, yet its effect on electrocardiogram (ECG)-based detection of type 1 and type 2 diabetes is poorly defined. AIMTo investigate whether cardiac comorbidity differentially influences machine-learning detection of the two diabetes types from single-lead ECG. METHODSIn this study, 2591 observations remained after exclusion of an erroneous age entry and rerunning the analytical pipeline.Twenty-six XGBoost models were evaluated separately for type 1 and type 2 diabetes within subgroups defined by seven cardiac-status criteria.Primary models used 47 single-lead ECG features and five anthropometric variables and were evaluated with five-fold stratified cross-validation.A post hoc seven-predictor sensitivity analysis assessed model complexity.Area under the receiver operating characteristics curve (AUC) uncertainty was estimated using 2000 bootstrap resamples of out-of-fold predictions, and ΔAUC comparisons were adjusted using the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure.Calibration was assessed using Brier score, calibration intercept and slope, reliability plots, and decision-curve analysis.Validation was observation-level because a persistent patient identifier was not available in the analytical export. RESULTSAfter correction and full rerun, median AUC was 0.693 for type 1 diabetes (range: 0.660-0.804)and 0.661 for type 2 diabetes (range: 0.543-0.716).No cardiac-pathology ΔAUC comparison remained statistically significant after Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment; the 5 / 45 smallest adjusted P value was 0.064.In the reduced seven-predictor sensitivity analysis, AUC was higher than the 52-predictor model in 17 of 26 evaluable subgroup models, with a median descriptive difference of +0.008.Calibration was suboptimal: Across the 26 models, calibration slopes ranged from 0.078 to 0.467 and intercepts from -1.287 to -0.535.Decision-curve analysis showed threshold-dependent net benefit rather than uniform superiority across the evaluated range. CONCLUSIONSingle-lead ECG combined with anthropometric information showed moderate internal discrimination for recorded diabetes status, but the corrected analysis did not identify a cardiac-pathology subgroup effect that remained significant after multiplicity adjustment.The reduced-feature sensitivity analysis suggested that similar discrimination may be achievable with fewer predictors, whereas calibration remained inadequate for direct interpretation of model outputs as disease probabilities.These findings do not establish a clinically validated screening or rule-out threshold.Patientgrouped validation, independent threshold validation, and external validation remain necessary before clinical implementation.

title: Early Valve Replacement vs Surveillance in Moderate Aortic Stenosis: Meta-Analysis of Randomized and Observational Evidence
authors: Ali Majed; Pia Kmeid; Ayah Safa; Hamza Kahwaji; Hashem Safieddine; Georges Ghanem
abstract: BACKGROUND: Moderate aortic stenosis (AS) is associated with excess mortality, and 2 randomized trials have tested early transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). OBJECTIVES: The authors sought to estimate the effects of early TAVR vs clinical surveillance and to compare randomized with observational estimates. METHODS: Six databases and registries were searched through November 3, 2026. Adjusted observational studies were synthesized separately from trials. Certainty was rated with GRADE. RESULTS: Two trials (922 patients; TAVR UNLOAD, n = 178, HF with reduced ejection fraction; PROGRESS, n = 744, 96.4% symptomatic) and 7 cohorts were included. Early TAVR did not detectably change death over approximately 2 years (HR: 1.05; 95% CI: 0.74-1.49; low certainty), with one-fifth of the deaths needed to detect a 20% reduction. Heart failure (HF) hospitalization was lower (RR: 0.53; 95% CI: 0.36-0.77; low certainty), or 70 fewer patients per 1,000 at 2 years. New pacemakers were more frequent (PROGRESS: 17.3% vs 9.3%; moderate certainty). About half of surveillance patients underwent valve replacement within 2 years. Observational cohorts estimated a 48% mortality reduction (HR: 0.52; 95% CI: 0.43-0.64; very low certainty), which differed from the randomized estimate (ratio of HRs: 2.01; 95% CI: 1.37-2.95). CONCLUSIONS: In older, predominantly symptomatic patients with moderate AS, early TAVR may make little or no difference to 2-year mortality and may reduce HF hospitalization, at the cost of more pacemakers. Because about half of patients under surveillance receive a valve within 2 years, the decision largely concerns timing. Observational survival estimates should not guide practice.

title: Risk-benefit assessment of oral anticoagulation in atrial fibrillation using virtual clinical trials
authors: Minsi Cai; Fateme Farahani; Michiel Rienstra; Stefano Severi; Harry J.G.M. Crijns; Ulrich Schotten; Jordi Heijman
abstract: Abstract Background: Oral anticoagulation (OAC) reduces stroke risk in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF), and screening can enable earlier AF detection and OAC initiation. However, the population-level trade-off between stroke prevention and OAC-related major bleeding for different types of AF and OAC therapy remains uncertain, and large randomized trials to resolve this are costly and time-consuming. Methods: A state-transition Markov-like model was developed to: 1) simulate the lifetime course of AF, stroke, major bleeding, and death in different virtual populations; 2) quantify benefits (stroke reduction) and harms (major bleeding) of systematic AF screening with screening-triggered OAC across CHA2DS2-VA scores; and 3) compare rhythm-guided, time-delimited ("pill-in-pocket") OAC with continuous OAC. Results: The model synthesized information from multiple clinical sources and reproduced stroke and bleeding incidence across clinical scenarios. At CHA?DS?-VA=2, long-term continuous rhythm monitoring (LT-CRM) with OAC lowered stroke risk (HR, 0.92 [95%CI, 0.88-0.96]) but raised bleeding risk (HR, 1.17 [95%CI, 1.07-1.27]) versus no screening. Time-to-benefit was shorter than time-to-harm for CHA?DS?-VA?4, but longer for CHA?DS?-VA=0. Pill-in-pocket OAC vs continuous OAC showed no difference in stroke/mortality (HR, 1.03, 95%CI [0.91-1.16]) but lower bleeding risk (HR, 0.81, 95%CI: 0.68-0.96]) in patients with elevated bleeding risk, but not at baseline. Sensitivity analyses revealed that the risk-benefit profiles of screening or pill-in-pocket OAC strategy further depend on OAC adherence and bleeding risks. Conclusions: Our model highlights a trade-off between stroke reduction and bleeding for systematic screening-initiated OAC, with net benefit for CHA?DS?-VA?4. We provide the first virtual implementation of an ongoing rhythm-guided OAC trial, showing that pill-in-pocket OAC may lower bleeding risk compared to continuous OAC, highlighting the potential of virtual clinical trials to guide clinical trial design.

title: Treatment of a concealed accessory pathway by radiofrequency catheter ablation in a horse
authors: Eva Buschmann; Glenn Van Steenkiste; Lize‐Maria Verhaeghe; Lennert Heirman; Stijn Schauvliege; Annelies Decloedt; Gunther van Loon
abstract: BACKGROUND: Accessory pathways (APs) are myocardial bundles directly connecting the atria and the ventricles, bypassing the atrioventricular node-His-Purkinje system. Retrograde AP conduction in horses can result in orthodromic atrioventricular re-entry tachycardia or bradycardia. Radiofrequency catheter ablation (RFCA) can provide a permanent treatment by eliminating the retrograde conducting AP, but was previously unsuccessful in one case. OBJECTIVES: To report the use of three-dimensional electro-anatomical mapping (3D EAM) to identify a concealed AP and treatment by RFCA in a horse. STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective case report. CASE DESCRIPTION: An irregular heart rhythm was detected in a 4-year-old, 518 kg Paint mare as an incidental finding. Frequent atrial depolarisations were identified in the ST segment with a fixed coupling interval to the preceding QRS complex on the ECG. A differential diagnosis of frequent premature atrial complexes displayed as bigeminy or a retrograde conduction along an AP was made. The presence of a retrograde conducting AP was confirmed by ventricular pacing, which resulted in 1:1 ventriculo-atrial activation. Three-dimensional EAM revealed the earliest atrial activation and thereby the atrial insertion of the AP in the caudal left atrium. Subsequent RFCA at 40 W eliminated AP conduction. MAIN LIMITATIONS: Single case report. CONCLUSIONS: This case report describes the identification of an AP by 3D EAM and the first successful permanent treatment of a retrograde conducting AP by RFCA in an adult horse.

title: Biomarker Testing, Imaging, and Outcomes in Cardiology-Referred Acute Breathlessness: A Retrospective Clinical Audit
authors: Jishel Mathews; Rana Kashif Riaz; Ayesha Kazi; Shamim Rahman
abstract: Background Breathlessness is a leading cause of emergency hospital attendances, and its multifactorial nature often reflects overlapping cardiopulmonary pathologies such as pulmonary embolism (PE), heart failure (HF), and acute coronary syndrome (ACS). Computed tomography pulmonary angiography (CTPA) is frequently used, often without documented pretest probability assessments. This audit primarily assessed the diagnostic yield of CTPA for suspected PE against the Royal College of Radiologists (RCR) standard of ≥15% and secondarily described biomarker testing, imaging, and outcomes across the PE, HF, and ACS pathways in patients referred to cardiology with acute breathlessness. Methods We conducted a retrospective audit of 70 adults referred to cardiology with breathlessness through the electronic patient record or multiprofessional team list (MPTL) referral systems at a district general hospital in the United Kingdom between March 1 and June 30, 2025. Biomarker testing for D-dimer, N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP), and high-sensitivity troponin I (hs-TnI), together with imaging and outcomes, was reviewed and described across the PE, HF, and ACS pathways, with diagnostic yields restricted to CTPA for suspected PE and coronary angiography for suspected ACS. Yields were reported with Wilson 95% CIs and compared using exploratory Fisher's exact tests. Additional analyses examined biomarker concentrations by outcome and overlap in biomarker and imaging use. Results Seventy patients were included (median age, 69.5 years; 52.9% male). D-dimer, NT-proBNP, and hs-TnI were tested in 68.6%, 58.6%, and 81.4% of patients, respectively. Overall, seven of 54 CTPAs performed for suspected PE were positive (13.0%, 95% CI, 6.4-24.4), numerically below the RCR benchmark of ≥15%. A clinically relevant alternative diagnosis was reported in 44.4% (target, ≥50%), and pretest probability was documented in 22.2% (target, 100%). PE yield was 15.0% (6/40) among patients with an elevated D-dimer, 0% (0/4) among those with a normal D-dimer, and 10.0% (1/10) among those without D-dimer testing (p = 1.000 for both comparisons). Left ventricular systolic dysfunction (LVSD) was found on transthoracic echocardiography in 40.0% (8/20) of patients with elevated NT-proBNP, 23.1% (3/13) of those with non-elevated NT-proBNP, and 26.3% (5/19) of those without testing (p = 0.456 and p = 0.501, respectively). Of 47 patients with elevated hs-TnI, 10 (21.3%) underwent coronary angiography for suspected ACS, with percutaneous coronary intervention performed in four (40.0%). Overall, 29 of 57 patients tested (50.9%) had hs-TnI levels above the sex-specific 99th-percentile upper reference limit. Conclusions Cardiology-referred breathlessness frequently involved multiple biomarker and imaging pathways during the same admission. CTPA yield, alternative diagnosis rates, and pretest probability documentation fell below RCR standards. LVSD was more frequent with elevated NT-proBNP, although differences were not statistically significant. No hs-TnI comparison was possible because all patients undergoing angiography for suspected ACS had elevated levels. Given the small, single-center sample and selective imaging, these findings do not establish diagnostic accuracy or pathway effectiveness. Larger multicenter studies are needed. The findings support reviewing pretest probability documentation and investigation decisions, followed by reaudit against RCR standards.

title: AIFA monitoring registries as a strategic tool in the Italian HTA framework: evolution and policy implications
authors: Lorenzo Martellone; Andrea Zovi; Giacomo Polito
abstract: The AIFA (Agenzia Italiana del Farmaco) monitoring registries represent one of the most distinctive regulatory tools within the Italian pharmaceutical governance framework. Initially introduced to support the appropriate use of reimbursed medicines and pharmaceutical expenditure control, they have progressively evolved into an infrastructure linking access to medicines, reimbursement governance, managed entry agreements (MEAs), and real-world data collection. This article examines the evolution and the policy relevance of AIFA monitoring registries within the Italian Health Technology Assessment framework. Firstly, it outlines the legislative and regulatory milestones shaping the system, from the establishment of AIFA in 2003 to the publication of the 2024 guideline, which formally defined the criteria for registry activation. Secondly, it describes the registry types, the criteria guiding their establishment, and the role of MEAs within the monitoring process. Thirdly, it provides an updated overview of the current registry landscape based on AIFA lists, identifying 340 closed registries (March 2026) and 366 active registries (April 2026), with “registri propriamente detti” (comprehensive registries) representing the predominant tool. Among those registries, MEAs were applied in nearly half of cases, with payment by result being the commonest scheme. The article also reviews the use of registry-derived data in peer-reviewed studies across hematology, oncology, cardiovascular diseases, and infectious diseases. Finally, it discusses key challenges, including duplication of information, limited interoperability with healthcare databases, administrative burden and residual discretion in registry activation despite recent transparency reforms. Overall, AIFA monitoring registries emerge as a strategic interface between pharmaceutical regulation, reimbursement governance, and evidence generation.

title: AI-driven multi-horizon risk stratification for heart failure hospitalization in UA with HFpEF: a Chinese multi-center cohort study
authors: Liying Huang; Yijun Wang; Mengdie Liu; Wenyuan Yin; Yonglian Chen; Tongjian Zhu; Jiajun Zhu; Bowen Zhou; Jun Wang; Jinhui Wu
abstract: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) complicated by unstable angina (UA) represents a major challenge in chronic disease management with high risk of recurrent heart failure hospitalization (HFH), and despite the availability of multicenter real-world data, AI-driven tools for multi-horizon risk assessment remain limited. This multicenter retrospective cohort enrolled 4367 patients with UA and HFpEF, and an ensemble feature selection pipeline integrating LASSO, SVM-RFE and Boruta identified robust predictors, followed by training of twelve machine learning algorithms to estimate HFH risk at 12-, 24- and 36-month horizons with external validation. The optimal time-specific models (ET, GBDT and LightGBM) achieved strong discrimination in the training cohort with AUCs of 0.818, 0.834 and 0.863, and maintained performance in external validation with AUCs of 0.839, 0.836 and 0.851, respectively, while SHAP analysis highlighted diabetes mellitus, TyG-BMI and NT-proBNP as the most influential predictors. We developed and externally validated a multi-time-point machine learning framework for HFH risk stratification in UA and HFpEF, which showed acceptable calibration and potential clinical utility on decision-curve analysis. Further prospective and real-world validation across diverse populations and healthcare systems is needed to confirm clinical effectiveness and support translation into routine practice.
